"""Bounded recovery after a scope exit or an interrupted CLI session."""

import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import (  # noqa: E402
    CleanupAction, CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, ContextLossAction,
    EditBlock, SessionLossAction,
)
from fortinet.common.common import FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature, StaticFeature  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.terminal import Data  # noqa: E402


IP_COMMAND = "set ip 10.0.52.4/24"
ACCESS_COMMAND = "set allowaccess ping https ssh http"


class RecordingFeature(Feature):
    def __init__(self, commander, block, context_action=None):
        super().__init__(None, commander, "management")
        self.block = block
        self.context_action = context_action
        self.losses = []
        self.attempts = []
        self.executed = []

    def activate(self):
        self.commander.submit_block(self, self.block)

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)
        self.attempts.append(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
        self.executed.append(attempt.spec.line)

    def on_context_loss(self, attempt):
        self.losses.append(attempt)
        if self.context_action is not None:
            return self.context_action
        return super().on_context_loss(attempt)


class RecoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def make_commander(self, *, continue_on_error=False, ip_command=IP_COMMAND,
                       context_action=None, following=False):
        terminal = MagicMock()
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), continue_on_error)
        block = ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
            ip_command, ACCESS_COMMAND,
        ])])
        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, block, context_action)
        features = [feature]
        if following:
            features.append(RecordingFeature(
                commander, CommandSequence("following", ["get system status"])
            ))
        commander.start(features)
        return commander, terminal, feature

    def prompt(self, commander, context=None):
        scope = f" ({context})" if context else ""
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT, Data(
            f"FGT-VM64-KVM-NSVHDM{scope} (Interim)#".encode()
        ))

    def enter_interface(self, commander):
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
        self.prompt(commander, "port1")

    def finish_interface(self, commander):
        self.prompt(commander, "port1")  # IP succeeds; dispatch allowaccess.
        self.prompt(commander, "port1")  # allowaccess succeeds; dispatch next.
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")  # next succeeds; dispatch end.
        self.prompt(commander)  # end succeeds.

    @staticmethod
    def writes(terminal):
        return [call.args[0] for call in terminal.write.call_args_list]

    def reconnect(self, commander):
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED, Data(b"Welcome!"))
        self.prompt(commander)

    def test_scope_exit_replays_openers_before_retrying_the_failed_command(self):
        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander)  # set ip unexpectedly returns to the VDOM shell.
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [
            "config system interface\r", "edit port1\r", IP_COMMAND + "\r",
            "config system interface\r",
        ])
        self.assertNotIn(IP_COMMAND, feature.executed)
        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].prompt_context_before, ("port1", "Interim"))
        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].prompt_context_after, ("Interim",))
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.finish_interface(commander)
        ip_attempts = [item for item in feature.attempts if item.spec.line == IP_COMMAND]
        self.assertEqual([item.retry_count for item in ip_attempts], [0, 1])
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)

    def test_repeated_context_loss_obeys_retry_limit_and_bootstrap_error_policy(self):
        for best_effort in (False, True):
            with self.subTest(best_effort=best_effort):
                commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander(
                    continue_on_error=best_effort, following=True,
                )
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.enter_interface(commander)
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.enter_interface(commander)
                if best_effort:
                    self.prompt(commander)
                    self.assertIn("retry limit", commander.feature_errors[0][1])
                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get system status\r")
                else:
                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "retry limit"):
                        self.prompt(commander)
                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 2)
                self.assertNotIn(ACCESS_COMMAND + "\r", self.writes(terminal))
                self.assertFalse(feature.completed)

    def test_session_and_context_loss_share_the_same_command_retry_allowance(self):
        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.reconnect(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "retry limit"):
            self.prompt(commander)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].retry_count, 1)

    def test_repeated_session_loss_waits_for_login_before_best_effort_skip(self):
        commander, terminal, _feature = self.make_commander(
            continue_on_error=True, following=True,
        )
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.reconnect(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost again"))
        self.assertNotIn("get system status\r", self.writes(terminal))
        self.reconnect(commander)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get system status\r")
        self.assertIn("retry limit", commander.feature_errors[0][1])

    def test_login_without_welcome_resumes_replay_and_exhaustion_handling(self):
        commander, terminal, _feature = self.make_commander(
            continue_on_error=True, following=True,
        )
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.prompt(commander)  # Successful login returns a prompt, no Welcome.
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "config system interface\r")
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost again"))
        self.assertNotIn("get system status\r", self.writes(terminal))
        self.prompt(commander)  # Exhaustion is handled at this usable prompt.
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get system status\r")
        self.assertIn("retry limit", commander.feature_errors[0][1])

    def test_each_command_position_gets_one_recovery(self):
        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander)  # First loss: IP command.
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander, "port1")  # IP succeeds; dispatch allowaccess.
        self.prompt(commander)  # Second loss: allowaccess command.
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.finish_interface(commander)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 3)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(ACCESS_COMMAND + "\r"), 2)

    def test_feature_can_decline_replay_without_running_session_loss_callback(self):
        for explicit_policy in (False, True):
            with self.subTest(explicit_policy=explicit_policy):
                spec = CommandSpec(IP_COMMAND, session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE)
                commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander(
                    ip_command=IP_COMMAND if explicit_policy else spec,
                    context_action=ContextLossAction.FAIL if explicit_policy else None,
                )
                feature.on_session_loss = MagicMock()
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.enter_interface(commander)
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "feature declined replay"):
                    self.prompt(commander)
                feature.on_session_loss.assert_not_called()
                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 1)

    def test_explicit_context_policy_can_allow_replay_independently_of_logout_policy(self):
        spec = CommandSpec(
            IP_COMMAND, session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
            context_loss=ContextLossAction.RESTART_BLOCK,
        )
        commander, _terminal, feature = self.make_commander(ip_command=spec)
        feature.on_session_loss = MagicMock()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.finish_interface(commander)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        feature.on_session_loss.assert_not_called()

    def test_partial_scope_is_aborted_once_before_replay(self):
        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")  # Only the edit context disappeared.
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "abort\r")
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "config system interface\r")
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.finish_interface(commander)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertNotIn("abort", feature.executed)
        self.assertNotIn("abort", [item.spec.line for item in feature.attempts])

    def test_failed_context_reset_does_not_loop(self):
        commander, terminal, _feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Unable to restore CLI context"):
            self.prompt(commander, "interface")
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count("abort\r"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 1)

    def test_session_loss_during_context_reset_resumes_after_login(self):
        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.reconnect(commander)
        self.enter_interface(commander)
        self.finish_interface(commander)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count("abort\r"), 1)

    def test_cleanup_session_loss_is_bounded(self):
        terminal = MagicMock()
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, CommandSequence("work", ["get status"]))
        commander.register_cleanup(feature, CleanupAction(
            "cleanup", CommandSequence("cleanup", ["get cleanup"]),
        ))
        commander.start([feature])
        self.prompt(commander)
        self.prompt(commander)  # Begin cleanup after the feature completes.
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.reconnect(commander)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "retry limit"):
            commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count("get cleanup\r"), 2)

    def test_newly_submitted_block_resets_retry_allowance(self):
        terminal = MagicMock()
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
        feature = StaticFeature(None, commander, "two-blocks", [
            ConfigBlock("system global", ["set alias first"]),
            ConfigBlock("system global", ["set alias second"]),
        ])
        commander.start([feature])
        self.prompt(commander)
        for _index in range(2):
            self.prompt(commander, "global")
            self.prompt(commander)  # Lost context: retry this block.
            self.prompt(commander, "global")
            self.prompt(commander, "global")
            self.prompt(commander)  # End this block and start the next one.
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count("set alias first\r"), 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count("set alias second\r"), 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Scope commit failures are mandatory errors, including best-effort commands."""

import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import (  # noqa: E402
    CleanupAction, CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, EditBlock,
)
from fortinet.common.common import FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.terminal import Data  # noqa: E402


class RecordingFeature(Feature):
    def __init__(self, commander, name, commands):
        super().__init__(None, commander, name)
        self.commands = commands
        self.executed = []

    def activate(self):
        self.commander.submit_block(self, CommandSequence(self.name, self.commands))

    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
        self.executed.append(attempt.spec.line)


class ScopeCommitFailureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @staticmethod
    def prompt(commander, context=None, output=b""):
        scope = f" ({context})" if context else ""
        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT, Data(
            output + f"fw{scope} #".encode()
        ))

    @staticmethod
    def writes(terminal):
        return [call.args[0] for call in terminal.write.call_args_list]

    def test_closing_failure_cannot_be_disabled_or_replayed(self):
        for close in ("next", "end"):
            for capture in (False, True):
                for best_effort in (False, True):
                    with self.subTest(close=close, capture=capture, best_effort=best_effort):
                        terminal = MagicMock()
                        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), best_effort)
                        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", [
                            CommandSpec(close, capture_output=capture, fail_on_error=False),
                            "set must-not-run 1",
                        ])
                        feature.on_context_loss = MagicMock()
                        following = RecordingFeature(commander, "following", ["get status"])
                        commander.start([feature, following])
                        self.prompt(commander, "port1")
                        # The failure code can span multiple serial reads.
                        for chunk in (b"Command fa", b"il. Return co", b"de -542.\r\n"):
                            data = Data(chunk)
                            commander.on_output(data)
                            self.assertTrue(data.discarded)
                        if best_effort:
                            self.prompt(commander, "interface")
                            self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [close + "\r", "get status\r"])
                            self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors[0][0], "commit")
                            self.assertIn("return code -542", commander.feature_errors[0][1])
                        else:
                            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "return code -542"):
                                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
                            self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [close + "\r"])
                        feature.on_context_loss.assert_not_called()
                        self.assertEqual(feature.executed, [])
                        self.assertFalse(feature.completed)

    def test_closing_failure_with_same_prompt_still_ejects(self):
        for code in ("0", "7", "-61"):
            for suffix in ("", "."):
                with self.subTest(code=code, suffix=suffix):
                    terminal = MagicMock()
                    commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
                    feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", ["next", "end"])
                    commander.start([feature])
                    self.prompt(commander, "port1")
                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, f"return code {code}"):
                        self.prompt(
                            commander, "port1",
                            f"  Command fail. Return code {code}{suffix}\r\n".encode(),
                        )
                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), ["next\r"])

    def test_tolerated_set_failure_does_not_poison_successful_scope_close(self):
        for capture in (False, True):
            with self.subTest(capture=capture):
                terminal = MagicMock()
                commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
                feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "configure", [
                    ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
                        CommandSpec("set unsupported 1", capture_output=capture),
                    ])]),
                ])
                commander.start([feature])
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
                self.prompt(commander, "port1")
                self.prompt(commander, "port1", b"Command fail. Return code -61.\r\n")
                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "next\r")
                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
                self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
                self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors, ())

    def test_cleanup_closing_failure_uses_bootstrap_error_policy(self):
        for best_effort in (False, True):
            with self.subTest(best_effort=best_effort):
                terminal = MagicMock()
                commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), best_effort)
                feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "work", ["get initial"])
                following = RecordingFeature(commander, "following", ["get status"])
                commander.register_cleanup(feature, CleanupAction(
                    "close", CommandSequence("close", ["end"]),
                ))
                commander.start([feature, following])
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.prompt(commander)
                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "end\r")
                if best_effort:
                    self.prompt(commander, output=b"Command fail. Return code -5.\r\n")
                    self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors[0][0], "cleanup")
                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get status\r")
                else:
                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "return code -5"):
                        self.prompt(commander, output=b"Command fail. Return code -5.\r\n")
                    self.assertNotIn("get status\r", self.writes(terminal))

    def test_unusable_completion_prompt_cannot_enter_best_effort_wait(self):
        terminal = MagicMock()
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), continue_on_error=True)
        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", [CommandSpec(
            "end", completion_states=(FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION,),
            expected_completion_state=FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT,
        )])
        commander.start([feature])
        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "unexpected prompt"):
            commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION, Data(b"Do you want to continue?"))
        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), ["end\r"])
        self.assertFalse(feature.completed)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Serial terminal buffering and FortiOS CLI state-machine tests."""

import logging
import re
import sys
import threading
import unittest
from contextlib import contextmanager
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

REPO_ROOT = __import__("pathlib").Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import CommandAttempt, CommandSpec  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.common import Credentials, FOSCliState, TRACE_LEVEL  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver import (  # noqa: E402
    FOSCliDriver,
    KernelPanicError,
)
from fortinet.common.terminal import Data, Terminal, _ByteQueue, terminal_buffer_limit_bytes  # noqa: E402


class ByteQueueTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_put_get_close_timeout_and_failure(self):
        queue = _ByteQueue(3)
        queue.put(b"abc")
        self.assertEqual(queue.get_one(), b"abc")
        queue.put(b"def")
        self.assertEqual(queue.get(), b"def")
        self.assertEqual(queue.get(0), b"")
        queue.close()
        queue.put(b"ignored")
        self.assertEqual(queue.get(), b"")
        failed = _ByteQueue(5)
        failed.fail(ValueError("read failed"))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "read failed"):
            failed.get(0)

    def test_blocked_get_wakes_when_data_arrives(self):
        queue = _ByteQueue(10)
        result = []
        reader = threading.Thread(target=lambda: result.append(queue.get(1)))
        reader.start()
        queue.put(b"ready")
        reader.join(1)
        self.assertEqual(result, [b"ready"])


class TerminalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def terminal_with_data(self, data, limit=100):
        terminal = Terminal(MagicMock(), MagicMock())
        terminal._buffer_limit = limit
        terminal._read_queue = _ByteQueue(limit)
        terminal._read_queue.put(data)
        terminal._ensure_reader = lambda: None
        return terminal

    def test_data_wrapper_and_expect_earliest_match_preserves_tail(self):
        view = Data(b"hello")
        self.assertTrue(view)
        self.assertEqual(len(view), 5)
        self.assertIn(b"ell", view)
        self.assertEqual(view.decode(), "hello")
        self.assertTrue(view.startswith(b"he"))
        self.assertEqual(view, b"hello")
        terminal = self.terminal_with_data(b"prefix PROMPT trailing")
        index, match, output = terminal.expect([b"trailing", b"PROMPT"], timeout=0.1)
        self.assertEqual(index, 1)
        self.assertEqual(match.group(), b"PROMPT")
        self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"prefix PROMPT")
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b" trailing")
        no_match = self.terminal_with_data(b"abc")
        result = no_match.expect([b"never"], timeout=0)
        self.assertEqual(result[0:2], (-1, None))
        self.assertEqual(bytes(result[2]), b"")

    def test_discard_retained_prefix_and_buffer_limit_error(self):
        terminal = self.terminal_with_data(b"output prompt", limit=20)
        _, _, _ = terminal.expect([b"prompt"], timeout=0.1)
        data = Data(b"output", terminal._discard_prefix)
        terminal._buffer = bytearray(b"output trailing")
        data.discard(b"output")
        self.assertTrue(data.discarded)
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b" trailing")
        data.discard(b"wrong")
        terminal._buffer = bytearray(b"123456")
        terminal._buffer_limit = 5
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "exceeded 5"):
            terminal._enforce_buffer_limit()
        terminal._logger.error.assert_called_once()

    def test_timeout_preserves_partial_token_for_a_later_read(self):
        terminal = self.terminal_with_data(b"Login incor")
        pattern = rb"(?m)^Login incorrect\r?$"
        index, match, output = terminal.expect([pattern], timeout=0.001)
        self.assertEqual((index, match), (-1, None))
        self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"Login incor")
        # Inspection without discard keeps the partial token, including when
        # another wait expires without receiving any more bytes.
        _, _, output = terminal.expect([pattern], timeout=0)
        self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"Login incor")
        terminal._read_queue.put(b"rect\n")
        index, match, output = terminal.expect([pattern], timeout=0.1)
        self.assertEqual(index, 0)
        self.assertEqual(match.group(), b"Login incorrect")
        self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"Login incorrect")
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"\n")

    def test_timeout_inspection_sees_a_token_completed_by_new_input(self):
        terminal = self.terminal_with_data(b"Verifying pass")
        _, _, output = terminal.expect([b"fw #"], timeout=0.001)
        self.assertIsNone(re.search(rb"Verifying password", bytes(output)))

        terminal._read_queue.put(b"word...\n")
        _, match, output = terminal.expect([b"fw #"], timeout=0.001)
        self.assertIsNone(match)
        self.assertIsNotNone(re.search(rb"Verifying password", bytes(output)))
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"Verifying password...\n")
        output.discard()
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"")

    def test_timeout_capture_consumes_retained_prefix_and_new_bytes(self):
        prefix = b"\nVerifying password...\n"
        chunk = b"admin\nadmin\n"
        terminal = self.terminal_with_data(chunk)
        terminal._buffer.extend(prefix)

        _, _, output = terminal.expect([b"fw #"], timeout=0.001)
        self.assertEqual(bytes(output), prefix + chunk)
        attempt = CommandAttempt(CommandSpec("end"), 1, 0)
        attempt.on_output(output)

        self.assertEqual(bytes(attempt.output), prefix + chunk)
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"")
        terminal._logger.warning.assert_not_called()

    def test_suppression_is_nested_and_restores_context(self):
        @contextmanager
        def context():
            events.append("enter")
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                events.append("exit")
        events = []
        connection = MagicMock()
        connection.suppress_output.return_value = context()
        terminal = Terminal(connection, MagicMock())
        with terminal.suppress_output():
            with terminal.suppress_output():
                self.assertEqual(terminal._output_suppression_depth, 2)
        self.assertEqual(events, ["enter", "exit"])
        self.assertIsNone(terminal._output_suppression_context)

    def test_write_and_close_flushes_writer(self):
        connection = MagicMock()
        terminal = Terminal(connection, MagicMock())
        terminal.write("hello")
        terminal.write(b" world")
        terminal.close()
        written = b"".join(call.args[0] for call in connection.write.call_args_list)
        self.assertEqual(written, b"hello world")
        connection.close.assert_called_once()

    def test_reader_failure_propagates_and_terminal_buffer_setting(self):
        reader = MagicMock()
        reader.read_very_eager.side_effect = OSError("serial failed")
        logger = MagicMock()
        terminal = Terminal(reader, logger)
        stop = threading.Event()
        queue = _ByteQueue(10)
        terminal._read_forever(stop, queue)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(OSError, "serial failed"):
            queue.get(0)
        logger.exception.assert_called_once()
        with patch.dict("os.environ", {"FOS_TERMINAL_BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES": "32"}):
            self.assertEqual(terminal_buffer_limit_bytes(), 32)
        with patch.dict("os.environ", {"FTNT_TERMINAL_BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES": "64", "FOS_TERMINAL_BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES": "32"}, clear=True):
            self.assertEqual(terminal_buffer_limit_bytes(), 64)
        with patch.dict("os.environ", {"FTNT_TERMINAL_BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES": "0"}, clear=True):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                terminal_buffer_limit_bytes()

    def test_raw_serial_log_uses_ftnt_name_and_legacy_fos_alias(self):
        for env_name in ("FTNT_LOG_RAW_SERIAL", "FOS_LOG_RAW_SERIAL"):
            with self.subTest(env_name=env_name):
                terminal = self.terminal_with_data(b"matched")
                with patch.dict("os.environ", {env_name: "true"}, clear=True):
                    terminal.expect([b"matched"], timeout=0.1)
                terminal._logger.log.assert_called_once_with(
                    TRACE_LEVEL,
                    "buffer: bytearray(b'matched')",
                )


class DriverTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def make_driver(self, *, allow_recovery=False):
        terminal, commander, logger = MagicMock(), MagicMock(), MagicMock()
        commander.ready = False
        creds = Credentials("admin", "old")
        blank = MagicMock()
        bootstrap = MagicMock()
        driver = FOSCliDriver(terminal, commander, creds, logger, "new", blank, bootstrap, allow_recovery)
        return driver, terminal, commander, logger, blank, bootstrap

    def test_prompt_patterns_responses_and_state_callbacks(self):
        driver, terminal, commander, logger, blank, bootstrap = self.make_driver()
        driver.set_prompt_patterns("lab[1]")
        self.assertIsNotNone(re.search(driver.state_patterns[FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT.value], b"lab[1] #"))
        self.assertIsNotNone(re.search(driver.state_patterns[FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT.value], b"lab[1] #\r"))
        driver._provide_username()
        driver._provide_password()
        driver._provide_current_password()
        driver._provide_new_password()
        driver._confirm_new_password()
        driver._continue_pager()
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_args_list[0].args[0], b"admin\r")
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_args_list[-1].args[0], b" ")
        self.assertTrue(driver._pending_bootstrap_activation)
        driver._credential_accepted()
        bootstrap.assert_called_once()
        driver._process_state(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO, Data(b"hostname # get"))
        commander.on_prompt_echo.assert_called_once()
        self.assertEqual(commander.on_state.call_count, 0)
        driver._process_state(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT, Data(b"hostname #"))
        commander.tick.assert_called()
        driver._last_known_state = FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT
        driver._current_state = FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT
        driver._process_state(FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT, Data(b""))
        commander.on_idle_prompt.assert_called_once()
        self.assertTrue(driver.at_command_prompt)

    def test_blank_fallback_and_previous_credential_recovery(self):
        driver, terminal, commander, logger, blank, bootstrap = self.make_driver(allow_recovery=True)
        driver._credential_rejected()
        driver._provide_password()
        blank.assert_called_once()
        self.assertFalse(driver._blank_fallback_available)
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_args.args[0], b"\r")
        driver.remember_current_credentials()
        driver._credential_rejected()
        driver._provide_username()
        driver._provide_password()
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_args_list[-2].args[0], b"admin\r")
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_args_list[-1].args[0], b"old\r")
        driver._credential_accepted()
        commander.record_feature_error.assert_called_once()
        driver._credential_accepted()
        commander.resolve_feature_error.assert_called_once()

    def test_rejected_and_recovery_credential_branches(self):
        driver, terminal, commander, logger, blank, bootstrap = self.make_driver()
        driver._initial_login_complete = True
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Credential rejected"):
            driver._credential_rejected()
        driver._license_failed()
        driver._last_known_state = FOSCliState.REBOOTING
        driver._unknown()
        self.assertEqual(driver._idle_spins, 1)
        driver._unknown_started_at = 0
        with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.time.monotonic", side_effect=[31, 32, 64, 65, 96, 97]):
            driver._recover_unknown_stall()
            driver._recover_unknown_stall()
            driver._recover_unknown_stall()
        self.assertEqual(terminal.write.call_count, 3)
        driver._unknown_newlines = 3
        driver._unknown_started_at = 1
        with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.time.monotonic", return_value=40):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "unknown state"):
                driver._recover_unknown_stall()
        driver._clear_unknown_stall()
        self.assertIsNone(driver._unknown_started_at)

    def test_state_selection_and_timeout_processing(self):
        driver, terminal, commander, logger, *_ = self.make_driver()
        terminal.expect.return_value = (FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME.value, re.search(b"login", b"login"), Data(b"login"))
        state, output, matched = driver._next_state()
        self.assertEqual(state, FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME)
        self.assertTrue(matched)
        terminal.expect.return_value = (-1, None, Data(b"noise"))
        self.assertEqual(driver._next_state()[0], FOSCliState.UNKNOWN)
        terminal.expect.return_value = (-1, None, Data(b""))
        self.assertEqual(driver._next_state()[0], FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT)
        driver._handle_state(FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_REJECTED)

    def test_retained_timeout_output_does_not_count_as_fresh_input(self):
        driver, _, _, logger, *_ = self.make_driver()
        terminal = Terminal(MagicMock(), logger)
        terminal._ensure_reader = lambda: None
        terminal._read_queue.put(b"partial token")
        driver._terminal = terminal

        with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.001):
            state, output, matched = driver._next_state()
            self.assertEqual(state, FOSCliState.UNKNOWN)
            self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"partial token")
            self.assertFalse(matched)
            state, output, matched = driver._next_state()
            self.assertEqual(state, FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT)
            self.assertEqual(bytes(output), b"partial token")
            self.assertFalse(matched)

    def test_kernel_panic_requires_kernel_diagnostic_and_raises(self):
        driver, terminal, commander, *_ = self.make_driver()
        pattern = driver.state_patterns[FOSCliState.KERNEL_PANIC.value]
        panic = (
            b"Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs\r\n"
            b"CPU: 0 PID: 1 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 4.19.13 #1\r\n"
        )

        self.assertIsNone(
            re.search(
                pattern,
                b"Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs",
            )
        )
        match = re.search(pattern, panic)
        self.assertIsNotNone(match)
        terminal.expect.return_value = (
            FOSCliState.KERNEL_PANIC.value,
            match,
            Data(panic),
        )

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(KernelPanicError, "Kernel panic detected"):
            driver.process_state()

        commander.on_state.assert_called_once_with(FOSCliState.KERNEL_PANIC, Data(panic))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

406:         self._inflight.prompt_context_before = self._prompt_context

409:             self._cleanup_retries.get(id(spec), 0)

427:         self._inflight = None

430:         attempt.prompt_context_after = self._prompt_context

440:                 self._dispatch_next()

443:             self._validate_completion(attempt, state)

446:                 # An interactive prompt cannot safely advance to another feature.

449:             if self._pending_feature_error is not None:

452:         if self._in_cleanup:
453:             self._cleanup_retries.pop(id(attempt.spec), None)

456:             return
457:         if self._is_standard_output_command(attempt.spec):
458:             self._complete_standard_output_command(attempt)

463:             return
464:         completed_feature = self._active_feature

474:     @staticmethod
475:     def _validate_completion(attempt, state):
476:         if (attempt.spec.closes_scope or attempt.spec.fail_on_error) and (
477:             failure := COMMAND_FAILURE_PATTERN.search(bytes(attempt.output))

480:                 f"FortiOS command {attempt.spec.line!r} failed "
481:                 f"(return code {failure.group(1).decode()})"
482:             )
483:         expected = attempt.spec.expected_completion_state
484:         if expected is not None and state != expected:

487:                 f"expected {expected.name}, received {state.name}"

490:     def _prompt_context_changed(self, attempt):
491:         before = attempt.prompt_context_before
492:         after = attempt.prompt_context_after

494:             before is not None
495:             and after is not None
496:             and before != after

500:     def _handle_context_loss(self, attempt):

610:     def _handle_session_loss(self):

615:         attempt = self._inflight
616:         self._inflight = None

622:             self._in_context_reset = False

624:         if self._in_cleanup:
625:             retries = self._cleanup_retries.get(id(attempt.spec), 0)
626:             if retries >= self.MAX_COMMAND_RECOVERY_RETRIES:

628:                     f"Session lost repeatedly during cleanup {attempt.spec.line!r}; "
629:                     "retry limit reached"
630:                 ))

632:             self._cleanup_retries[id(attempt.spec)] = retries + 1
633:             self._cleanup.appendleft(attempt.spec)
634:             self._in_cleanup = False
635:             return
636:         self._schedule_feature_cleanup(self._active_feature, "interruption")
637:         action = self._call_feature(
638:             self._active_feature.on_session_loss,
639:             attempt,
640:         )
641:         if self._pending_feature_error is not None:
642:             return
643:         self.logger.info(
644:             f"Session lost during {self._active_feature.name}/{attempt.spec.line!r}; {action.name.lower()}"

654:             ),
655:             SessionLossAction.VALIDATE: lambda: self._pending.clear(),

import logging
import re
import time
from .common import (
    FOSCliState,
    FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS,
    BOOTSTRAP_HOSTNAME_REGEX,
    PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX,
    TRACE_LEVEL,
)


PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS = 10
EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1
UNKNOWN_STALL_SECONDS = 30
UNKNOWN_STALL_NEWLINE_LIMIT = 3


class KernelPanicError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the guest kernel reports a panic on the serial console."""


class FOSCliDriver:
    """Owns serial reads and delegates command dispatch to the commander."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        terminal,
        commander,
        credentials,
        logger,
        bootstrap_password,
        activate_blank_credentials,
        activate_bootstrap_credentials,
        allow_credential_recovery=False,
    ):
        self._terminal = terminal
        self._commander = commander
        self._logger = logger
        self._state_patterns = FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS.copy()
        self._last_known_state = FOSCliState.UNKNOWN
        self._current_state = FOSCliState.UNKNOWN
        self._last_logged_state = None
        self._idle_spins = 0
        self._credentials = credentials
        self._bootstrap_password = bootstrap_password
        self._activate_blank_credentials = activate_blank_credentials
        self._activate_bootstrap_credentials = activate_bootstrap_credentials
        self._allow_credential_recovery = allow_credential_recovery
        self._recovery_credentials = None
        self._recovery_attempted = False
        self._use_recovery_credentials = False
        self._blank_fallback_available = True
        self._send_blank_password = False
        self._initial_login_complete = False
        self._awaiting_login_acceptance = False
        self._credential_recovery_pending = False
        self._pending_bootstrap_activation = False
        self._unknown_started_at = None
        self._unknown_newlines = 0
        self._state_handlers = {
            FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME: self._provide_username,
            FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD: self._provide_password,
            FOSCliState.CURRENT_PASSWORD: self._provide_current_password,
            FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD: self._provide_new_password,
            FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD_CONFIRM: self._confirm_new_password,
            FOSCliState.MORE_PROMPT: self._continue_pager,
            FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED: self._credential_accepted,
            FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT: self._command_prompt,
            FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO: None,
            FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_REJECTED: self._credential_rejected,
            FOSCliState.LIC_FAIL: self._license_failed,
            FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT: self._timeout,
            FOSCliState.KERNEL_PANIC: self._kernel_panic,
            FOSCliState.UNKNOWN: self._unknown,
        }

    @property
    def state_patterns(self):
        return self._state_patterns

    @property
    def ready(self):
        return self._commander.ready

    def remember_current_credentials(self):
        """Keep the last accepted credentials for a failed password transition."""
        if self._recovery_credentials is not None or self._recovery_attempted:
            return
        self._recovery_credentials = (
            self._credentials.username,
            self._credentials.password,
        )
        self._recovery_attempted = False

    @property
    def at_command_prompt(self):
        """Whether the most recent console event left FortiOS at a CLI prompt."""
        return self._current_state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT or (
            self._current_state == FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT
            and self._last_known_state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT
        )

    def process_state(self):
        spin_start = time.time()
        while not self.ready and time.time() < spin_start + PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS:
            state, output, matched = self._next_state()
            self._current_state = state
            if output and not matched:
                self._commander.on_output(output)
                if state == FOSCliState.UNKNOWN:
                    self._note_unknown_output()
                output = type(output)(b"")
            if state.value < FOSCliState.UNKNOWN.value:
                self._idle_spins = 0
                self._last_known_state = state
                self._clear_unknown_stall()
                self._log_state(state)
            self._process_state(state, output)

    def _log_state(self, state):
        if state == FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT:
            return
        if state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT and self._last_logged_state == state:
            return
        self._last_logged_state = state
        self._logger.debug(f"ST: {state.name}")

    def _process_state(self, state, output):
        """Handle a CLI state and then let the commander observe it.

        A password confirmation can be followed immediately by a command
        prompt, without ``Welcome!``.  Apply that credential transition
        before the commander dispatches the command associated with the
        prompt.
        """
        if state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT:
            self._handle_state(state)
        if state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO:
            self._commander.on_prompt_echo(output)
        else:
            self._commander.on_state(state, output)
        if state != FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT:
            self._handle_state(state)
        if state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT:
            self._commander.tick()
        elif state == FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT and self._last_known_state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT:
            self._commander.tick()
            self._commander.on_idle_prompt()

    def _next_state(self):
        index, match, output = self._terminal.expect(self._state_patterns, EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
        if match:
            return FOSCliState(index), output, True
        # A timeout exposes retained bytes too. Only fresh input should reset
        # the unknown-output stall timer; an unchanged buffer is still idle.
        state = FOSCliState.UNKNOWN if output.received_new_data else FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT
        return state, output, False

    def _handle_state(self, state):
        handler = self._state_handlers.get(state)
        if handler:
            try:
                handler()
            except Exception:
                self._logger.exception("CLI state handler failed for %s", state.name)
                raise

    def _provide_username(self):
        username = self._credentials.username
        if self._use_recovery_credentials and self._recovery_credentials is not None:
            username = self._recovery_credentials[0]
        self._awaiting_login_acceptance = True
        self._respond(FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME, username)

    def _provide_password(self):
        if self._send_blank_password:
            # The initial blank-password fallback is consumed as soon as it is
            # sent. Later credential recovery is managed separately.
            self._send_blank_password = False
            self._blank_fallback_available = False
            self._activate_blank_credentials()
            self._respond(FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD, b"")
            return
        if self._use_recovery_credentials and self._recovery_credentials is not None:
            self._respond(
                FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD,
                self._recovery_credentials[1],
            )
            return
        self._respond(FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD, self._credentials.password)

    def _provide_current_password(self):
        self._respond(FOSCliState.CURRENT_PASSWORD, self._credentials.password)

    def _provide_new_password(self):
        self._respond(FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD, self._bootstrap_password)

    def _confirm_new_password(self):
        self._respond(FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD_CONFIRM, self._bootstrap_password)
        # Do not update active credentials until FortiOS accepts the
        # confirmation. A rejected confirmation leaves the active password
        # unchanged so that subsequent prompts use the right value.
        self._pending_bootstrap_activation = True

    def _continue_pager(self):
        self._terminal.write(b" ")

    def _credential_accepted(self):
        self._accept_login()

    def _accept_login(self):
        self._initial_login_complete = True
        self._awaiting_login_acceptance = False
        recovered = (
            self._use_recovery_credentials
            and self._recovery_credentials is not None
        )
        if recovered:
            self._use_recovery_credentials = False
            self._recovery_attempted = False
            if not self._credential_recovery_pending:
                self._commander.record_feature_error(
                    "admin-credentials",
                    "desired credentials were rejected; resumed with the previous credentials "
                    "while keeping the desired credentials for later logins",
                )
            self._credential_recovery_pending = True
        elif self._recovery_credentials is not None:
            self._recovery_attempted = False
            if self._credential_recovery_pending:
                self._commander.resolve_feature_error(
                    "admin-credentials",
                    "the desired credentials authenticated successfully",
                )
                self._credential_recovery_pending = False
        self._activate_pending_bootstrap_credentials()

    def _command_prompt(self):
        """Accept password confirmation on versions that skip ``Welcome!``."""
        if self._awaiting_login_acceptance:
            self._accept_login()
        else:
            self._initial_login_complete = True
            self._activate_pending_bootstrap_credentials()

    def _activate_pending_bootstrap_credentials(self):
        if self._pending_bootstrap_activation:
            self._activate_bootstrap_credentials()
            self._pending_bootstrap_activation = False

    @staticmethod
    def _license_failed():
        # SetLicense inspects the buffered command output when FortiOS returns
        # to a prompt. Raising here would interrupt the driver at LIC_FAIL,
        # before best-effort bootstrap can safely skip the feature.
        return None

    def _timeout(self):
        self._idle_spins += 1
        self._recover_unknown_stall()

    def _unknown(self):
        if self._last_known_state == FOSCliState.REBOOTING:
            self._idle_spins += 1

    @staticmethod
    def _kernel_panic():
        raise KernelPanicError("Kernel panic detected on serial console")

    def _note_unknown_output(self):
        self._unknown_started_at = time.monotonic()

    def _recover_unknown_stall(self):
        if self._unknown_started_at is None:
            return
        if time.monotonic() - self._unknown_started_at < UNKNOWN_STALL_SECONDS:
            return
        if self._unknown_newlines >= UNKNOWN_STALL_NEWLINE_LIMIT:
            raise RuntimeError("CLI remained in unknown state")
        self._unknown_newlines += 1
        self._unknown_started_at = time.monotonic()
        self._logger.warning(
            "CLI stuck in unknown state; sending newline "
            f"({self._unknown_newlines}/{UNKNOWN_STALL_NEWLINE_LIMIT})"
        )
        self._terminal.write(b"\r")

    def _clear_unknown_stall(self):
        self._unknown_started_at = None
        self._unknown_newlines = 0

    def set_prompt_patterns(self, name_pattern):
        if isinstance(name_pattern, str):
            name_pattern = re.escape(name_pattern.encode())
        self._state_patterns[FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME.value] = rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + name_pattern + rb"[ \t]+login:[ \t]*"
        self._state_patterns[FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT.value] = rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + name_pattern + PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX + rb"[ \t]*[#$][ \t]*\r?$"
        self._state_patterns[FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO.value] = rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + name_pattern + PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX + rb"[ \t]*[#$][ \t]*[^\r\n]+(?:\r?\n)?"

    def _credential_rejected(self):
        # A rejected interaction cannot establish the newly selected
        # bootstrap password.  Do not activate it on a later unrelated
        # acceptance or prompt.
        self._pending_bootstrap_activation = False
        if not self._initial_login_complete and self._blank_fallback_available:
            self._send_blank_password = True
            return
        if (
            self._allow_credential_recovery
            and self._recovery_credentials is not None
            and not self._recovery_attempted
        ):
            self._recovery_attempted = True
            self._use_recovery_credentials = True
            self._logger.warning(
                "Credentials were rejected; retrying with the previously accepted credentials"
            )
            return
        raise RuntimeError("Credential rejected")

    def _respond(self, state, response):
        """Write an interactive response to the CLI."""
        if isinstance(response, str):
            response = response.encode()
        self._logger.log(
            TRACE_LEVEL,
            "Responding to CLI state %s with '%s'",
            state.name,
            response,
        )
        self._terminal.write(bytes(response) + b"\r")

parts.text:
Now I understand the Data/expect semantics:

- On match: consumed bytes (up to match end) removed from buffer, returned as `Data(consumed)` with NO discard callback. So consumers don't need to discard matched output; it's already gone.
- On timeout: full unmatched buffer returned as Data with `_discard_prefix` callback; buffer retains it unless a consumer discards.

`CommandAttempt.on_output` captures and discards when `capture_output or closes_scope`. So a capturing command's `attempt.output` gets bytes exactly once per byte, because:
- unmatched output (timeout) → driver forwards once → attempt.on_output appends + discards from buffer.
- matched output → expect already removed those bytes from buffer; Data has no discard callback; attempt.on_output appends bytes(output) and calls output.discard(data) — with no callback, discard just sets discarded=True, harmless.

But wait — driver line 109-113: `if output and not matched: commander.on_output(output); output = type(output)(b"")`. Then `_process_state(state, output)` with empty Data. For state UNKNOWN/TN_TIMEOUT, commander.on_state is called with empty Data → on_output(empty) returns early. Good, no duplication.

But what about matched output? In `process_state`, `if output and not matched:` — matched output is NOT forwarded to commander.on_output directly; instead `_process_state(state, output)` → `commander.on_state(state, output)` → inside on_state: `self.on_output(output)` (line 292). So matched Data reaches on_output once via on_state. Good.

However: there's a subtlety in `process_state` for unmatched: commander.on_output is called BEFORE the state handler; on_state is then called with empty Data. But for CMD_PROMPT matched, on_state gets full Data and calls on_output. Both paths invoke inflight/active feature on_output. What about the case where output is unmatched but state is UNKNOWN/TN_TIMEOUT and there IS an inflight capturing command: attempt.on_output appends and discards → buffer cleared. Good.

What if inflight exists but is NOT capturing (capture_output=False, not closes_scope) and active feature's on_output returns False → `_inspect_output`: discards only if `_recovering`. Otherwise bytes stay in buffer. Next expect timeout exposes them again → commander.on_output → again nothing consumes → buffer grows. With a capturing inflight they'd be captured. Non-capturing command with streaming junk output: buffer grows to 1MB limit → RuntimeError. That's by design ("Terminal buffer exceeded ... without being consumed"). Pre-existing behavior presumably.

Now the duplicate-processing concern: `received_new_data` flag distinguishes. SetLicense.on_output: `if LICENSE_FAILURE_PATTERN.search(output)` — output here is the Data view. +"""Admin credential commits followed by logout and console authentication."""
+
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
+
+from fortinet.common.common import Credentials
+from fortinet.common.features.credentials import CredentialsFeature
+from fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver import FOSCliDriver
+from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander
+from fortinet.common.terminal import Terminal
+from fortinet.tests.test_common_stack_parsing import RecordingFeature, SerialConnection
+
+
+LOGIN = b"fw login:\r\n"
+READY = b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n"
+ADMIN_PROMPT = b"fw (admin) #\r\n"
+
+
+class AdminCredentialsTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def make_stack(self, *, password="newpass", username="admin",
+                   auto_logout=None, authenticate=True, reject=False,
+                   exit_works=True):
+        logger = MagicMock()
+        policy_prompt = b"fw (password-policy) #\r\n"
+        old_password_responses = [READY]
+        if password:
+            old_password_responses.append(ADMIN_PROMPT)
+        old_password_responses.append(b"Login incorrect\r\n" + LOGIN)
+        end_count = 0
+
+        def end_response():
+            nonlocal end_count
+            end_count += 1
+            return LOGIN if auto_logout == "end" and end_count == 2 else b"fw #\r\n"
+
+        login_reply = None if not authenticate else (
+            b"Login incorrect\r\n" + LOGIN if reject else READY
+        )
+        responses = {
+            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
+            b"oldpass\r": lambda: old_password_responses.pop(0),
+            b"config system password-policy\r": policy_prompt,
+            b"set status disable\r": policy_prompt,
+            b"config system admin\r": ADMIN_PROMPT,
+            f"edit {username}\r".encode(): ADMIN_PROMPT,
+            b"set accprofile super_admin\r": ADMIN_PROMPT,
+            b"next\r": LOGIN if auto_logout == "next" else ADMIN_PROMPT,
+            b"end\r": end_response,
+            b"exit\r": LOGIN if exit_works else b"fw #\r\n",
+            b"probe\r": b"fw #\r\n",
+            (password + "\r").encode(): login_reply,
+        }
+        if username != "admin":
+            responses[(username + "\r").encode()] = b"Password:"
+        if password:
+            responses[f"set password {password}\r".encode()] = (
+                b"Please enter current administrator password: "
+            )
+        else:
+            responses[b"unset password\r"] = ADMIN_PROMPT
+
+        connection = SerialConnection(responses)
+        terminal = Terminal(connection, logger)
+        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, logger)
+        credentials = Credentials("admin", "oldpass")
+        driver = FOSCliDriver(
+            terminal, commander, credentials, logger, "bootstrap",
+            MagicMock(), MagicMock(), allow_credential_recovery=True,
+        )
+

+"""Bounded recovery after a scope exit or an interrupted CLI session."""
+
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
+
+from fortinet.common.cli_commands import (  # noqa: E402
+    CleanupAction, CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, ContextLossAction,
+    EditBlock, SessionLossAction,
+)
+from fortinet.common.common import FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
+from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature, StaticFeature  # noqa: E402
+from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
+from fortinet.common.terminal import Data  # noqa: E402
+
+
+IP_COMMAND = "set ip 10.0.52.4/24"
+ACCESS_COMMAND = "set allowaccess ping https ssh http"
+
+
+class RecordingFeature(Feature):
+    def __init__(self, commander, block, context_action=None):
+        super().__init__(None, commander, "management")
+        self.block = block
+        self.context_action = context_action
+        self.losses = []
+        self.attempts = []
+        self.executed = []
+
+    def activate(self):
+        self.commander.submit_block(self, self.block)
+
+    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
+        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)
+        self.attempts.append(attempt)
+
+    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
+        self.executed.append(attempt.spec.line)
+
+    def on_context_loss(self, attempt):
+        self.losses.append(attempt)
+        if self.context_action is not None:
+            return self.context_action
+        return super().on_context_loss(attempt)
+
+
+class RecoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def make_commander(self, *, continue_on_error=False, ip_command=IP_COMMAND,
+                       context_action=None, following=False):
+        terminal = MagicMock()
+        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), continue_on_error)
+        block = ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
+            ip_command, ACCESS_COMMAND,
+        ])])
+        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, block, context_action)
+        features = [feature]
+        if following:
+            features.append(RecordingFeature(
+                commander, CommandSequence("following", ["get system status"])
+            ))
+        commander.start(features)
+        return commander, terminal, feature
+
+    def prompt(self, commander, context=None):
+        scope = f" ({context})" if context else ""
+        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT, Data(
+            f"FGT-VM64-KVM-NSVHDM{scope} (Interim)#".encode()
+        ))
+
+    def enter_interface(self, commander):
+        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+        self.prompt(commander, "port1")
+
+    def finish_interface(self, commander):
+        self.prompt(commander, "port1")  # IP succeeds; dispatch allowaccess.
+        self.prompt(commander, "port1")  # allowaccess succeeds; dispatch next.
+        self.prompt(commander, "interface")  # next succeeds; dispatch end.
+        self.prompt(commander)  # end succeeds.
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def writes(terminal):
+        return [call.args[0] for call in terminal.write.call_args_list]
+
+    def reconnect(self, commander):
+        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED, Data(b"Welcome!"))
+        self.prompt(commander)
+
+    def test_scope_exit_replays_openers_before_retrying_the_failed_command(self):
+        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
+        self.prompt(commander)
+        self.enter_interface(commander)
+        self.prompt(commander)  # set ip unexpectedly returns to the VDOM shell.
+        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [
+            "config system interface\r", "edit port1\r", IP_COMMAND + "\r",
+            "config system interface\r",
+        ])
+        self.assertNotIn(IP_COMMAND, feature.executed)
+        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].prompt_context_before, ("port1", "Interim"))
+        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].prompt_context_after, ("Interim",))
+        self.enter_interface(commander)
+        self.finish_interface(commander)
+        ip_attempts = [item for item in feature.attempts if item.spec.line == IP_COMMAND]
+        self.assertEqual([item.retry_count for item in ip_attempts], [0, 1])
+        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
+        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
+
+    def test_repeated_context_loss_obeys_retry_limit_and_bootstrap_error_policy(self):
+        for best_effort in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(best_effort=best_effort):
+                commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander(
+                    continue_on_error=best_effort, following=True,
+                )
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.enter_interface(commander)
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.enter_interface(commander)
+                if best_effort:
+                    self.prompt(commander)
+                    self.assertIn("retry limit", commander.feature_errors[0][1])
+                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get system status\r")
+                else:
+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "retry limit"):
+                        self.prompt(commander)
+                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 2)
+                self.assertNotIn(ACCESS_COMMAND + "\r", self.writes(terminal))
+                self.assertFalse(feature.completed)
+
+    def test_session_and_context_loss_share_the_same_command_retry_allowance(self):
+        commander, terminal, feature = self.make_commander()
+        self.prompt(commander)
+        self.enter_interface(commander)
+        commander.on_state(FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, Data(b"session lost"))
+        self.reconnect(commander)
+        self.enter_interface(commander)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "retry limit"):
+            self.prompt(commander)
+        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal).count(IP_COMMAND + "\r"), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(feature.losses[0].retry_count, 1)
+

+"""Scope commit failures are mandatory errors, including best-effort commands."""

+class RecordingFeature(Feature):
+    def __init__(self, commander, name, commands):
+        super().__init__(None, commander, name)
+        self.commands = commands
+        self.executed = []
+
+    def activate(self):
+        self.commander.submit_block(self, CommandSequence(self.name, self.commands))
+
+    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):

+            output + f"fw{scope} #".encode()
+        ))

+    @staticmethod

+        return [call.args[0] for call in terminal.write.call_args_list]

+                        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", [

+                            "set must-not-run 1",

+                        feature.on_context_loss = MagicMock()

+                        commander.start([feature, following])
+                        self.prompt(commander, "port1")
+                        # The failure code can span multiple serial reads.
+                        for chunk in (b"Command fa", b"il. Return co", b"de -542.\r\n"):
+                            data = Data(chunk)
+                            commander.on_output(data)
+                            self.assertTrue(data.discarded)
+                        if best_effort:
+                            self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+                            self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [close + "\r", "get status\r"])
+                            self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors[0][0], "commit")
+                            self.assertIn("return code -542", commander.feature_errors[0][1])
+                        else:

+                                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+                            self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), [close + "\r"])

+                        self.assertFalse(feature.completed)

+    def test_closing_failure_with_same_prompt_still_ejects(self):

+                    commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
+                    feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", ["next", "end"])
+                    commander.start([feature])

+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, f"return code {code}"):
+                        self.prompt(
+                            commander, "port1",
+                            f"  Command fail. Return code {code}{suffix}\r\n".encode(),
+                        )
+                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), ["next\r"])
+
+    def test_tolerated_set_failure_does_not_poison_successful_scope_close(self):
+        for capture in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(capture=capture):
+                terminal = MagicMock()
+                commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock())
+                feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "configure", [
+                    ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
+                        CommandSpec("set unsupported 1", capture_output=capture),
+                    ])]),
+                ])
+                commander.start([feature])
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+                self.prompt(commander, "port1")
+                self.prompt(commander, "port1", b"Command fail. Return code -61.\r\n")
+                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "next\r")
+                self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
+                self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
+                self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors, ())
+
+    def test_cleanup_closing_failure_uses_bootstrap_error_policy(self):
+        for best_effort in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(best_effort=best_effort):
+                terminal = MagicMock()
+                commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), best_effort)
+                feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "work", ["get initial"])
+                following = RecordingFeature(commander, "following", ["get status"])
+                commander.register_cleanup(feature, CleanupAction(
+                    "close", CommandSequence("close", ["end"]),
+                ))
+                commander.start([feature, following])
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.prompt(commander)
+                self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "end\r")
+                if best_effort:
+                    self.prompt(commander, output=b"Command fail. Return code -5.\r\n")
+                    self.assertEqual(commander.feature_errors[0][0], "cleanup")
+                    self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal)[-1], "get status\r")
+                else:
+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "return code -5"):
+                        self.prompt(commander, output=b"Command fail. Return code -5.\r\n")
+                    self.assertNotIn("get status\r", self.writes(terminal))
+
+    def test_unusable_completion_prompt_cannot_enter_best_effort_wait(self):
+        terminal = MagicMock()
+        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, MagicMock(), continue_on_error=True)
+        feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "commit", [CommandSpec(
+            "end", completion_states=(FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION,),
+            expected_completion_state=FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT,
+        )])
+        commander.start([feature])
+        self.prompt(commander, "interface")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "unexpected prompt"):
+            commander.on_state(FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION, Data(b"Do you want to continue?"))
+        self.assertEqual(self.writes(terminal), ["end\r"])
+        self.assertFalse(feature.completed)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
