"""End-to-end parsing from a serial connection through the FortiOS commander."""

import queue
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import (  # noqa: E402
    CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, EditBlock, SetValue,
)
from fortinet.common.common import Credentials, FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver import FOSCliDriver  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.terminal import Terminal  # noqa: E402


class SerialConnection:
    """A serial-like connection that answers each write with a byte stream."""

    def __init__(self, responses):
        self._incoming = queue.Queue()
        self._responses = responses
        self.writes = []
        self.closed = False
        self._incoming.put(b"fw login:\r\n")

    def read_very_eager(self):
        try:
            return self._incoming.get_nowait()
        except queue.Empty:
            return b""

    def write(self, data):
        data = bytes(data)
        self.writes.append(data)
        response = self._responses.get(data)
        if callable(response):
            response = response()
        if response:
            chunks = response if isinstance(response, (tuple, list)) else (response,)
            for chunk in chunks:
                if chunk:
                    self._incoming.put(bytes(chunk))

    def close(self):
        self.closed = True

    def suppress_output(self):
        from contextlib import nullcontext
        return nullcontext()


class RecordingFeature(Feature):
    def __init__(self, commander, name, commands):
        super().__init__(None, commander, name)
        self.commands = commands
        self.executed = []
        self.dispatched = []

    def activate(self):
        self.commander.submit_block(self, CommandSequence(self.name, self.commands))

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)
        self.dispatched.append(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
        self.executed.append((attempt.spec.line, bytes(attempt.output), state))


class FullStackParsingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def make_stack(self, features, responses, *, allow_credential_recovery=False):
        logger = MagicMock()
        connection = SerialConnection(responses)
        terminal = Terminal(connection, logger, default_wait="fw #")
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, logger)
        commander.start(features(commander))
        driver = FOSCliDriver(
            terminal=terminal,
            commander=commander,
            credentials=Credentials("admin", "secret"),
            logger=logger,
            bootstrap_password="Bootstrap1!",
            activate_blank_credentials=MagicMock(),
            activate_bootstrap_credentials=MagicMock(),
            allow_credential_recovery=allow_credential_recovery,
        )
        return connection, terminal, commander, driver

    def test_login_command_echo_multiline_output_and_continuation(self):
        result = b"".join([
            b"fw # show full-configuration system dns\r\n",
            b"config system dns\r\n",
            b"    set protocol dot\r\n",
            b"    set primary 9.9.9.9\r\n",
            b"end\r\n",
            b"fw #\r\n",
        ])
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n",
            b"show full-configuration system dns\r": result,
            b'set comment "first line\r': b">\r\n",
            b"second line\r": b">\r\n",
            b'third line"\r': b"fw #\r\n",
        }
        features = []

        def configured(commander):
            inspect = RecordingFeature(commander, "inspect", [
                CommandSpec("show full-configuration system dns", capture_output=True),
            ])
            multiline = RecordingFeature(commander, "multiline", [
                SetValue("comment", "first line\nsecond line\nthird line"),
            ])
            features.extend([inspect, multiline])
            return features

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        driver.process_state()

        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
        self.assertTrue(commander.startup_complete)
        self.assertTrue(all(feature.completed for feature in features))
        self.assertTrue(connection.closed)
        self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
            b"admin\r",
            b"secret\r",
            b"show full-configuration system dns\r",
            b'set comment "first line\r',
            b"second line\r",
            b'third line"\r',
        ])
        self.assertEqual(len(features[0].executed), 1)
        captured = features[0].executed[0][1]
        self.assertIn(b"set protocol dot", captured)
        self.assertIn(b"set primary 9.9.9.9", captured)
        self.assertEqual(features[0].executed[0][2], FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry[2] for entry in features[1].executed],
            [FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT, FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT],
        )
        self.assertTrue(all(attempt.output for attempt in features[1].dispatched))
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"")

    def test_mixed_prompt_context_and_pager_states_reach_feature_callbacks(self):
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw (global) #\r\n",
            b"get system status\r": (
                b"fw (global) # get system status\r\n"
                b"Version: FortiGate-VM64 v7.4.2,build2571\r\n"
                b"--More--\r\n"
                b"Serial-Number: FGVMTEST\r\n"
                b"fw (global) #\r\n"
            ),
            b" \r": b"fw (global) #\r\n",
        }
        feature_ref = []

        class PagerFeature(RecordingFeature):
            def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
                super().on_command_executed(attempt, state)
                self.commander.feature_complete(self)

        def configured(commander):
            feature = PagerFeature(commander, "status", [
                CommandSpec("get system status", capture_output=True),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, _terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        driver.process_state()

        feature = feature_ref[0]
        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
            b"admin\r", b"secret\r", b"get system status\r", b" ",
        ])
        captured = feature.executed[0][1]
        self.assertIn(b"FortiGate-VM64 v7.4.2,build2571", captured)
        self.assertIn(b"Serial-Number: FGVMTEST", captured)
        self.assertEqual(feature.executed[0][2], FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)
        self.assertEqual(driver._current_state, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)

    def test_aborted_interface_edit_recovers_through_serial_driver(self):
        ip_responses = iter([
            b"abort\r\nfw (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
        ])
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"config system interface\r": b"fw (interface) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"edit port1\r": b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r": lambda: next(ip_responses),
            b"set allowaccess ping https ssh http\r": b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"next\r": b"fw (interface) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"end\r": b"fw (Interim)#\r\n",
        }
        feature_ref = []

        def configured(commander):
            feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "management", [
                ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
                    "set ip 10.0.52.4/24", "set allowaccess ping https ssh http",
                ])]),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        try:
            driver.process_state()
            self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
            self.assertTrue(feature_ref[0].completed)
            self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
                b"admin\r", b"secret\r",
                b"config system interface\r", b"edit port1\r", b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r",
                b"config system interface\r", b"edit port1\r", b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r",
                b"set allowaccess ping https ssh http\r", b"next\r", b"end\r",
            ])
        finally:
            terminal.close()

    def test_failed_next_ejects_before_end_through_serial_driver(self):
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n",
            b"config system interface\r": b"fw (interface)#\r\n",
            b"edit port1\r": b"fw (port1)#\r\n",
            b"set unsupported 1\r": b"Command fail. Return code -61.\r\nfw (port1)#\r\n",
            b"next\r": (
                b"Command fa", b"il. Return code -5.\r\nfw (port1)#\r\n",
            ),
        }
        feature_ref = []

        def configured(commander):
            feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "management", [
                ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", ["set unsupported 1"])]),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        try:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "'next'.*return code -5"):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
                b"admin\r", b"secret\r", b"config system interface\r",
                b"edit port1\r", b"set unsupported 1\r", b"next\r",
            ])
            self.assertFalse(feature_ref[0].completed)
            self.assertFalse(commander.ready)
        finally:
            terminal.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Administrator bootstrap feature."""

from ..cli_commands import CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, EditBlock, SessionLossAction
from ..common import FOSCliState

from .base import StaticFeature


class CredentialsFeature(StaticFeature):
    """Configure the administrator, then log out and authenticate again."""

    def __init__(self, vm, commander):
        self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
        self._desired_credentials_activated = False
        self._password_change_committed = False
        credentials = vm.desired_credentials
        admin_children = ["set accprofile super_admin"]
        if credentials.password:
            admin_children.append(CommandSpec(
                f"set password {credentials.password}",
                session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
            ))
        elif credentials.username == "admin":
            admin_children.append(CommandSpec(
                "unset password", session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
            ))
        super().__init__(vm, commander, "admin", [
            ConfigBlock("system password-policy", ["set status disable"]),
            ConfigBlock("system admin", [EditBlock(credentials.username, admin_children)]),
            CommandSequence("admin-relogin", [CommandSpec(
                "exit",
                session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
                # A successful logout takes the session-loss path. Returning
                # straight to a CLI prompt must not count as verification.
                expected_completion_state=FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME,
            )]),
        ], on_complete=lambda: self._activate_desired_credentials())

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        if attempt.spec.line == "exit":
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)

    def on_session_loss(self, attempt):
        if attempt.spec.line == "exit":
            # The commander resumes this block only at the authenticated CLI
            # prompt. Clear the logout command so it cannot be replayed.
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._is_password_command(attempt.spec.line):
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._activate_after_admin_commit and attempt.spec.line == "next":
            # Some releases log out during the commit instead of returning
            # its CLI prompt. Authenticate with the committed password.
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            self._password_change_committed = True
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._password_change_committed:
            # FortiOS may log out as the admin edit closes. The password
            # command and `next` have already committed the new credentials,
            # so replaying this block would use the previous password again.
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        return super().on_session_loss(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, command, state):
        line = command.spec.line
        if self._is_password_command(line):
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = True
        elif self._activate_after_admin_commit and line == "next":
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            self._password_change_committed = True

    @staticmethod
    def _is_password_command(line):
        return line.startswith("set password ") or line == "unset password"

    def _activate_desired_credentials(self):
        if self._desired_credentials_activated:
            return
        self.vm.activate_desired_credentials()
        self._desired_credentials_activated = True

    CHANGE_PASSWORD = auto()
    CREDENTIAL_REJECTED = auto()
    CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED = auto()

    CONFIRMATION = auto()
    CHANGE_PASSWORD_CONFIRM = auto()
    MORE_PROMPT = auto()
    MULTILINE_PROMPT = auto()
    KERNEL_PANIC = auto()
    UNKNOWN = auto()  # Non-patterns from here on.
    TN_TIMEOUT = auto()


GENERIC_HOSTNAME_REGEX = rb"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+"
DEFAULT_HOSTNAME_REGEX = rb"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:-VM64)?-KVM(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]*)?"
LICENSED_HOSTNAME_REGEX = rb"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{7,}"
BOOTSTRAP_HOSTNAME_REGEX = (
    rb"(?:" + GENERIC_HOSTNAME_REGEX + rb"|" + DEFAULT_HOSTNAME_REGEX + rb"|" + LICENSED_HOSTNAME_REGEX + rb")"
)
PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX = rb"(?:[ \t]+\([^)]+\))*"
DEFAULT_HOSTNAME_PROMPT = rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + BOOTSTRAP_HOSTNAME_REGEX + PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX + rb"[ \t]*[#$][ \t]*\r?$"
DEFAULT_HOSTNAME_PROMPT_ECHO = rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + BOOTSTRAP_HOSTNAME_REGEX + PROMPT_CONTEXT_REGEX + rb"[ \t]*[#$][ \t]*[^\r\n]+(?:\r?\n)?"

FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS = [None] * FOSCliState.UNKNOWN.value
FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS[FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME.value] = (
        rb"(?m)^[ \t]*" + BOOTSTRAP_HOSTNAME_REGEX +
        rb"(?:\((?:Primary|Secondary)\))?"
        rb"[ \t]+login:[ \t]*"
)
FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS[FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD.value] = rb"(?m)^New Password:[ \t]*"
FOS_CLI_STATE_PATTERNS[FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD.value] = rb"(?m)^Password:[ \t]*"

"""Command and scope data used by the FortiOS CLI scheduler."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum, auto

from .common import FOSCliState


class SessionLossAction(Enum):
    RESTART_BLOCK = auto()
    COMPLETE_BLOCK = auto()
    CONTINUE = auto()
    VALIDATE = auto()
    FAIL = auto()


class ContextLossAction(Enum):
    RESTART_BLOCK = auto()
    FAIL = auto()


@dataclass(frozen=True, init=False)
class CommandSpec:
    line: str
    completion_states: tuple = ()
    capture_output: bool = False
    suppress_output: bool = False
    session_loss: SessionLossAction = SessionLossAction.RESTART_BLOCK
    expected_completion_state: object = None
    fail_on_error: bool = False
    context_loss: ContextLossAction = ContextLossAction.RESTART_BLOCK
    continuation: bool = False

    def __init__(self, line, completion_states=(), capture_output=False,
                 suppress_output=False, session_loss=SessionLossAction.RESTART_BLOCK,
                 expected_completion_state=None, fail_on_error=False,
                 context_loss=None, continuation=False):
        object.__setattr__(self, "line", line)
        object.__setattr__(self, "completion_states", completion_states)
        object.__setattr__(self, "capture_output", capture_output)
        object.__setattr__(self, "suppress_output", suppress_output)
        object.__setattr__(self, "session_loss", session_loss)
        object.__setattr__(self, "expected_completion_state", expected_completion_state)
        object.__setattr__(self, "fail_on_error", fail_on_error)
        object.__setattr__(self, "continuation", continuation)

def parse_log_level(value):
    if value is None or str(value).strip() == "":
        return logging.DEBUG
    value = str(value).strip()
    try:
        return int(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    normalized = value.upper()
    if normalized in LOG_LEVEL_NAMES:
        return LOG_LEVEL_NAMES[normalized]
    raise ValueError(
        "Invalid FOS_LOG_LEVEL. Use TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, "
        "another Python logging level name, or a numeric level."
    )


def exit_on_bootstrap_error(value=None):
    """Return whether a bootstrap exception should terminate the VM.

    Bootstrap failures are fatal by default.  The opt-out is intentionally
    narrow: only the explicit value ``false`` disables termination, so a
    misspelled or otherwise invalid value keeps the fail-fast behavior.
    """
    if value is None:
        value = get_env("FOS_EXIT_ON_BOOTSTRAP_ERROR", "true")
    return str(value).strip().lower() != "false"


def container_dns_servers(path="/etc/resolv.conf"):
    """Return nameserver addresses configured for this container, in order."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as resolver_config:
            servers = []
            for line in resolver_config:
                fields = line.split()
                if len(fields) >= 2 and fields[0] == "nameserver":
                    servers.append(fields[1])
            return servers
    except OSError:
        return []


def apply_debug_feature_cutoff(features, stop_feature, logger):
    """Limit bootstrap features to those up to and including ``stop_feature``."""
    if stop_feature is None or str(stop_feature).strip() == "":
        return features

    stop_feature = str(stop_feature).strip()
    for index, feature in enumerate(features):
        if feature.name == stop_feature:
            selected = features[:index + 1]
            skipped = features[index + 1:]
            logger.warning(
                "FOS_DEBUG_FEATURE=%s; stopping after feature %s. Skipping: %s",
                stop_feature,
                stop_feature,
                ", ".join(feature.name for feature in skipped) or "(none)",
            )
            return selected

    available = ", ".join(feature.name for feature in features)
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown FOS_DEBUG_FEATURE '{stop_feature}'. Available features: {available}")


class FortiOSConsole(vrnetlab._Console):
    def __init__(self, driver):
        super().__init__(driver)
        self._output_enabled = True

    def _read(self):
        data = self._driver.channel.read()
        if data and self._output_enabled:
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
        return data

    def read_very_eager(self):
        transport_socket = getattr(self._driver.transport, "socket", None)
        socket = getattr(transport_socket, "sock", None)
        if socket is not None:
            readable, _, _ = select.select([socket], [], [], 0)
            if not readable:
                return b""
        return self._read()

    def read_blocking(self):
        return self._read()

    @contextmanager
    def suppress_output(self):
        output_enabled = self._output_enabled
        self._output_enabled = False
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._output_enabled = output_enabled

"""Administrator bootstrap feature."""

from ..cli_commands import CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, EditBlock, SessionLossAction
from ..common import FOSCliState

from .base import StaticFeature


class CredentialsFeature(StaticFeature):
    """Configure the administrator, then log out and authenticate again."""

    def __init__(self, vm, commander):
        self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
        self._desired_credentials_activated = False
        self._password_change_committed = False
        credentials = vm.desired_credentials
        admin_children = ["set accprofile super_admin"]
        if credentials.password:
            admin_children.append(CommandSpec(
                f"set password {credentials.password}",
                session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
            ))
        elif credentials.username == "admin":
            admin_children.append(CommandSpec(
                "unset password", session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
            ))
        super().__init__(vm, commander, "admin", [
            ConfigBlock("system password-policy", ["set status disable"]),
            ConfigBlock("system admin", [EditBlock(credentials.username, admin_children)]),
            CommandSequence("admin-relogin", [CommandSpec(
                "exit",
                session_loss=SessionLossAction.CONTINUE,
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=True,
                # A successful logout takes the session-loss path. Returning
                # straight to a CLI prompt must not count as verification.
                expected_completion_state=FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME,
            )]),
        ], on_complete=lambda: self._activate_desired_credentials())

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        if attempt.spec.line == "exit":
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)

    def on_session_loss(self, attempt):
        if attempt.spec.line == "exit":
            # The commander resumes this block only at the authenticated CLI
            # prompt. Clear the logout command so it cannot be replayed.
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._is_password_command(attempt.spec.line):
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._activate_after_admin_commit and attempt.spec.line == "next":
            # Some releases log out during the commit instead of returning
            # its CLI prompt. Authenticate with the committed password.
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            self._password_change_committed = True
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        if self._password_change_committed:
            # FortiOS may log out as the admin edit closes. The password
            # command and `next` have already committed the new credentials,
            # so replaying this block would use the previous password again.
            return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE
        return super().on_session_loss(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, command, state):
        line = command.spec.line
        if self._is_password_command(line):
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = True
        elif self._activate_after_admin_commit and line == "next":
            self._activate_desired_credentials()
            self._activate_after_admin_commit = False
            self._password_change_committed = True

    @staticmethod
    def _is_password_command(line):
        return line.startswith("set password ") or line == "unset password"

    def _activate_desired_credentials(self):
        if self._desired_credentials_activated:
            return
        self.vm.activate_desired_credentials()
        self._desired_credentials_activated = True

1: """PKI certificate installation feature.
2: 
3: Installs CA certificates (trust), local certificate/key pairs, remote
4: certificates, and certificate revocation lists at bootstrap. Env variables
5: carry paths only; this feature reads the file contents and never logs or
6: stores the certificate, key, or password bytes themselves.
7: 
8: Entries are ``;``-separated and start with a reference-name field followed
9: by ``:`` (``refname:rest``). The refname becomes the FortiOS object name;
10: an empty refname field (``:rest``) implies the object name from the
11: certificate CN.
12: 
13: Env variables:
14: 
15: - ``FTNT_PKI_CA_CERTS``: ``refname:path`` — CAs installed in
16:   ``config vpn certificate ca`` and named by refname or CN.
17: - ``FTNT_PKI_LOCAL_CERTS``: ``refname:key_path:cert_path`` — installed as
18:   local certificate entries named by refname or CN, including the SSL
19:   deep-inspection CA pair (which is just a local cert). Both the private key
20:   and certificate are required.
21: - ``FTNT_PKI_LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES``: ``path;path;...`` — positionally paired
22:   with encrypted-key ``refname:key_path:cert_path`` entries; the contents
23:   are typed as ``set password``.
24: - ``FTNT_PKI_REMOTE_CERTS``: ``refname:path`` — remote certificates installed
25:   in ``config vpn certificate remote`` and named by refname or CN.
26: - ``FTNT_PKI_CRLS``: ``refname:path`` — CRLs installed as ``config vpn
27:   certificate crl`` entries with PEM contents when that tree is available,
28:   otherwise imported over TFTP, named by refname or file basename.
29: """
30: 
31: import os
32: import re
33: import shutil
34: import ssl
35: 
36: from ..cli_commands import (
37:     CommandSequence,
38:     CommandSpec,
39:     SetValue,

46: LOCAL_CERTS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_LOCAL_CERTS"
47: LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV = "FOS_PKI_LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES"
48: REMOTE_CERTS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_REMOTE_CERTS"
49: CRLS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_CRLS"
50: 
51: # The config tree moved back and forth between these names across releases.
52: VPN_CERTIFICATE_CRL_SCOPE = "vpn certificate crl"
53: TFTP_PKI_DIRECTORY = "/tftpboot/pki"
54: COMMAND_FAILURE_PATTERN = re.compile(
55:     rb"(?mi)Unknown action|command (?:parse )?error|Command fail"
56: )
57: 
58: 
59: def _split_entries(variable, value):
60:     """Split ``value`` on ``;`` and strip whitespace, dropping empty entries."""
61:     if value is None:
62:         return []
63:     return [entry for raw in value.split(";") if (entry := raw.strip())]
64: 
65: 
66: def _require_path(variable, path):
67:     if not os.path.exists(path):
68:         raise ValueError(f"{variable}: path does not exist: {path}")
69: 
70: 
71: def _split_refname(entry, variable):
72:     """Split the leading refname field from an entry.
73: 
74:     Every entry is ``refname:rest``; an empty refname field (``:rest``)
75:     means the object name is implied by the certificate CN.
76:     Returns ``(refname_or_None, rest)``.
77:     """
78:     refname, separator, rest = entry.partition(":")
79:     if not separator:
80:         raise ValueError(
81:             f"{variable}: entry '{entry}' must start with a refname field "
82:             "followed by ':'; use ':" + entry + "' to imply the "
83:             "certificate CN"
84:         )
85:     if not rest:
86:         raise ValueError(
87:             f"{variable}: entry '{entry}' must carry a path after the refname"
88:         )
89:     return refname or None, rest

92: def parse_ca_certs(value, variable=CA_CERTS_ENV):
93:     """Return ``(refname_or_None, path)`` pairs from ``value``."""
94:     parsed = []
95:     for refname, path in (
96:         _split_refname(entry, variable)
97:         for entry in _split_entries(variable, value)
98:     ):
99:         _require_path(variable, path)
100:         parsed.append((refname, path))
101:     return parsed

104: def parse_local_certs(value, variable=LOCAL_CERTS_ENV):
105:     """Return ``(refname_or_None, key_path, cert_path)`` triples.
106: 
107:     Entries are ``refname:key_path:cert_path``. The refname field is always
108:     present; ``:key_path:cert_path`` implies the certificate CN as the object
109:     name. Local certificates require their corresponding private key.
110:     """
111:     parsed = []
112:     for entry in _split_entries(variable, value):
113:         refname, rest = _split_refname(entry, variable)
114:         key_path, separator, cert_path = rest.partition(":")
115:         if not separator:

118:                 "certificate paths as 'refname:key_path:cert_path'; use "
119:                 "':key_path:cert_path' to imply the certificate CN"
120:             )

122:         _require_path(variable, cert_path)

127: def parse_pass_files(value, variable=LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV):

214:         self._paired_locals = self._pair_pass_files()

218:         self._indexes = {"ca": 0, "local": 0, "remote": 0, "crl": 0}

297:     @staticmethod
298:     def _config_item_block(scope, name, children):

302:         # opening commands keep ``fail_on_error`` enabled, the commander raises

376:                 validate_prompt=False,

379:             "local", name, cert_path,
380:             self._config_item_block("vpn certificate local", name, lines),

383: 
384:     def _submit_next_crl(self):

386:         if item is None:
387:             return False
388:         _index, (refname, path) = item
389:         name = refname or self._crl_basename(path)

391:             self._current_item = ("crl", name, path)

- ``FTNT_PKI_CA_CERTS``: ``refname:path`` — CAs installed in

- ``FTNT_PKI_LOCAL_CERTS``: ``refname:key_path:cert_path`` — installed as

  deep-inspection CA pair (which is just a local cert). Both the private key

"""PKI certificate installation feature.

Installs CA certificates (trust), local certificate/key pairs, remote
certificates, and certificate revocation lists at bootstrap. Env variables
carry paths only; this feature reads the file contents and never logs or
stores the certificate, key, or password bytes themselves.

Entries are ``;``-separated and start with a reference-name field followed
by ``:`` (``refname:rest``). The refname becomes the FortiOS object name;
an empty refname field (``:rest``) implies the object name from the
certificate CN.

Env variables:

- ``FTNT_PKI_CA_CERTS``: ``refname:path`` — CAs installed in
  ``config vpn certificate ca`` and named by refname or CN.
- ``FTNT_PKI_LOCAL_CERTS``: ``refname:key_path:cert_path`` — installed as
  local certificate entries named by refname or CN, including the SSL
  deep-inspection CA pair (which is just a local cert). Both the private key
  and certificate are required.
- ``FTNT_PKI_LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES``: ``path;path;...`` — positionally paired
  with encrypted-key ``refname:key_path:cert_path`` entries; the contents
  are typed as ``set password``.
- ``FTNT_PKI_REMOTE_CERTS``: ``refname:path`` — remote certificates installed
  in ``config vpn certificate remote`` and named by refname or CN.
- ``FTNT_PKI_CRLS``: ``refname:path`` — CRLs installed as ``config vpn
  certificate crl`` entries with PEM contents when that tree is available,
  otherwise imported over TFTP, named by refname or file basename.
"""

import os
import re
import shutil
import ssl

from ..cli_commands import (
    CommandSequence,
    CommandSpec,
    SetValue,
)
from ..env import get_env
from .base import Feature


CA_CERTS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_CA_CERTS"
LOCAL_CERTS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_LOCAL_CERTS"
LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV = "FOS_PKI_LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES"
REMOTE_CERTS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_REMOTE_CERTS"
CRLS_ENV = "FOS_PKI_CRLS"

# The config tree moved back and forth between these names across releases.
VPN_CERTIFICATE_CRL_SCOPE = "vpn certificate crl"
TFTP_PKI_DIRECTORY = "/tftpboot/pki"
COMMAND_FAILURE_PATTERN = re.compile(
    rb"(?mi)Unknown action|command (?:parse )?error|Command fail"
)


def _split_entries(variable, value):
    """Split ``value`` on ``;`` and strip whitespace, dropping empty entries."""
    if value is None:
        return []
    return [entry for raw in value.split(";") if (entry := raw.strip())]


def _require_path(variable, path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise ValueError(f"{variable}: path does not exist: {path}")


def _split_refname(entry, variable):
    """Split the leading refname field from an entry.

    Every entry is ``refname:rest``; an empty refname field (``:rest``)
    means the object name is implied by the certificate CN.
    Returns ``(refname_or_None, rest)``.
    """
    refname, separator, rest = entry.partition(":")
    if not separator:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{variable}: entry '{entry}' must start with a refname field "
            "followed by ':'; use ':" + entry + "' to imply the "
            "certificate CN"
        )
    if not rest:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{variable}: entry '{entry}' must carry a path after the refname"
        )
    return refname or None, rest


def parse_ca_certs(value, variable=CA_CERTS_ENV):
    """Return ``(refname_or_None, path)`` pairs from ``value``."""
    parsed = []
    for refname, path in (
        _split_refname(entry, variable)
        for entry in _split_entries(variable, value)
    ):
        _require_path(variable, path)
        parsed.append((refname, path))
    return parsed


def parse_local_certs(value, variable=LOCAL_CERTS_ENV):
    """Return ``(refname_or_None, key_path, cert_path)`` triples.

    Entries are ``refname:key_path:cert_path``. The refname field is always
    present; ``:key_path:cert_path`` implies the certificate CN as the object
    name. Local certificates require their corresponding private key.
    """
    parsed = []
    for entry in _split_entries(variable, value):
        refname, rest = _split_refname(entry, variable)
        key_path, separator, cert_path = rest.partition(":")
        if not separator:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{variable}: entry '{entry}' must include private key and "
                "certificate paths as 'refname:key_path:cert_path'; use "
                "':key_path:cert_path' to imply the certificate CN"
            )
        _require_path(variable, key_path)
        _require_path(variable, cert_path)
        parsed.append((refname, key_path, cert_path))
    return parsed


def parse_pass_files(value, variable=LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV):
    entries = _split_entries(variable, value)
    for entry in entries:
        _require_path(variable, entry)
    return entries


def parse_remote_certs(value, variable=REMOTE_CERTS_ENV):
    """Return ``(refname_or_None, path)`` pairs from ``value``."""
    parsed = []
    for refname, path in (
        _split_refname(entry, variable)
        for entry in _split_entries(variable, value)
    ):
        _require_path(variable, path)
        parsed.append((refname, path))
    return parsed


def parse_crls(value, variable=CRLS_ENV):
    """Return ``(refname_or_None, path)`` pairs from ``value``."""
    parsed = []
    for refname, path in (
        _split_refname(entry, variable)
        for entry in _split_entries(variable, value)
    ):
        _require_path(variable, path)
        parsed.append((refname, path))
    return parsed


def read_certificate_cn(path):
    """Read the subject CN from a PEM certificate file.

    Uses ``ssl._ssl._test_decode_cert``; a minimal DER header scan is the
    fallback for builds where the private API is unavailable. Raises
    ``ValueError`` naming the file when the CN cannot be determined.
    """
    try:
        if hasattr(ssl._ssl, "_test_decode_cert"):
            decoded = ssl._ssl._test_decode_cert(path)
            for rdn in decoded.get("subject", ()):
                for attribute, value in rdn:
                    if attribute == "commonName":
                        return value
        raise ValueError(f"Could not read certificate CN from {path}")
    except ValueError:
        raise
    except Exception as error:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not read certificate CN from {path}: {error}")


def read_pass_file(path):
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as password:
        contents = password.read().strip()
    if not contents:
        raise ValueError(f"{LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV}: empty password file: {path}")
    return contents


def read_crl_body(path):
    """Return the CRL file contents for ``set crl``.

    FortiOS documents the field as "Certificate Revocation List as a PEM
    file": type the full PEM, headers included. Re-encoding the body a
    second time is rejected by 7.4+ with return code -542.
    """
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as crl:
        return crl.read()


class InstallPkiCertificates(Feature):
    """Install certificates and CRLs provided by the plugin before startup config.

    Must run after the factory baseline capture and before the user startup
    config so the config can reference the installed certificate names.
    """

    def __init__(self, vm, commander):
        super().__init__(vm, commander, "pki-certificates")
        self._logger = commander.logger
        self._tftp_server_ip = vm.mgmt_gw_ipv4
        self._ca_paths = parse_ca_certs(get_env(CA_CERTS_ENV))
        self._local_entries = parse_local_certs(get_env(LOCAL_CERTS_ENV))
        self._pass_files = parse_pass_files(get_env(LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV))
        self._remote_paths = parse_remote_certs(get_env(REMOTE_CERTS_ENV))
        self._crl_paths = parse_crls(get_env(CRLS_ENV))
        self._paired_locals = self._pair_pass_files()
        self._staging_directory = TFTP_PKI_DIRECTORY
        self._phase = "idle"
        self._crl_config = None
        self._indexes = {"ca": 0, "local": 0, "remote": 0, "crl": 0}
        self._seen_names = {"ca": set(), "local": set(), "remote": set(), "crl": set()}
        self._current_item = None
        self._config_failed = False
        self._fallback_active = False

    def _pair_pass_files(self):
        """Pair pass files positionally with local entries that carry a key."""
        if len(self._pass_files) > len(self._local_entries):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{LOCAL_CERT_PASS_FILES_ENV} has more entries than "
                f"{LOCAL_CERTS_ENV}; cannot pair passwords"
            )
        paired = []
        for index, (refname, key_path, cert_path) in enumerate(self._local_entries):
            pass_file = self._pass_files[index] if index < len(self._pass_files) else None
            paired.append((refname, key_path, cert_path, pass_file))
        return paired

    def activate(self):
        if not self._blocks_ready():
            self.commander.feature_complete(self)
            return
        version = self.vm.fos_version
        if version is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "FortiOS version is unavailable; image-info must run "
                "before pki-certificates"
            )
        self._crl_config = self._crl_config_from_major(version.major)
        self._phase = "start"
        self._submit_next()

    def _blocks_ready(self):
        return bool(self._ca_paths or self._local_entries or self._remote_paths or self._crl_paths)

    def _local_with_password(self):
        return self._paired_locals

    def _submit_next(self):
        if self._phase == "start":
            self._phase = "ca-certs"
        if self._phase == "ca-certs":
            if self._submit_next_ca_cert():
                return
            self._phase = "local-certs"
        if self._phase == "local-certs":
            if self._submit_next_local_cert():
                return
            self._phase = "remote-certs"
        if self._phase == "remote-certs":
            if self._submit_next_remote_cert():
                return
            self._phase = "crl-config"
        if self._phase == "crl-config":
            if self._submit_next_crl():
                return
        self.commander.feature_complete(self)

    def _next_entry(self, kind, entries):
        index = self._indexes[kind]
        if index >= len(entries):
            return None
        self._indexes[kind] += 1
        return index, entries[index]

    def _begin_config_item(self, kind, name, path, block):
        if name in self._seen_names[kind]:
            self._logger.warning(
                "Duplicate %s certificate name '%s'; last entry wins",
                kind.upper() if kind == "ca" else kind,
                name,
            )
        self._seen_names[kind].add(name)
        self._current_item = (kind, name, path)
        self._config_failed = False
        self._fallback_active = False
        self.commander.submit_block(self, block)

    @staticmethod
    def _config_item_block(scope, name, children):
        # A configuration attempt is deliberately best-effort: the feature
        # must be able to inspect the result and fall back to the TFTP import
        # path when a firmware release does not expose this config tree.  If
        # opening commands keep ``fail_on_error`` enabled, the commander raises
        # before ``on_command_executed`` can select that fallback. A return-code
        # failure from `next` or `end` is always fatal to the feature: the
        # commander checks scope commits even when fail_on_error is disabled.
        def config_command(line):
            return CommandSpec(line, capture_output=True, fail_on_error=False)

        return CommandSequence(f"{scope}-{name}", [
            config_command(f"config {scope}"),
            config_command(f'edit "{name}"'),
            *children,
            config_command("next"),
            config_command("end"),
        ])

    def _submit_next_ca_cert(self):
        item = self._next_entry("ca", self._ca_paths)
        if item is None:
            return False
        _index, (refname, path) = item
        name = refname or read_certificate_cn(path)
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as certificate:
            value = SetValue(
                "ca", certificate.read(),
                fail_on_error=False,
                validate_prompt=False,
            )
        self._begin_config_item(
            "ca", name, path,
            self._config_item_block("vpn certificate ca", name, [value]),
        )
        return True

    def _submit_next_remote_cert(self):
        item = self._next_entry("remote", self._remote_paths)
        if item is None:
            return False
        _index, (refname, path) = item
        name = refname or read_certificate_cn(path)
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as certificate:
            value = SetValue(
                "remote", certificate.read(),
                fail_on_error=False,
                validate_prompt=False,
            )
        self._begin_config_item(
            "remote", name, path,
            self._config_item_block("vpn certificate remote", name, [value]),
        )
        return True

    def _submit_next_local_cert(self):
        item = self._next_entry("local", self._local_with_password())
        if item is None:
            return False
        _index, (refname, key_path, cert_path, pass_file) = item
        name = refname or read_certificate_cn(cert_path)
        lines = []
        if pass_file:
            lines.append(CommandSpec(
                f"set password {read_pass_file(pass_file)}",
                capture_output=True,
                fail_on_error=False,
            ))
        with open(key_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as key:
            lines.append(SetValue(
                "private-key", key.read(),
                fail_on_error=False,
                validate_prompt=False,
            ))
        with open(cert_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as cert:
            lines.append(SetValue(
                "certificate", cert.read(),
                fail_on_error=False,
                validate_prompt=False,
            ))
        self._begin_config_item(
            "local", name, cert_path,
            self._config_item_block("vpn certificate local", name, lines),
        )
        return True

    def _submit_next_crl(self):
        item = self._next_entry("crl", self._crl_paths)
        if item is None:
            return False
        _index, (refname, path) = item
        name = refname or self._crl_basename(path)
        if self._crl_config is None:
            self._current_item = ("crl", name, path)
            self._config_failed = True
            self._submit_tftp_fallback()
            return True
        value = SetValue("crl", read_crl_body(path))
        self._begin_config_item(
            "crl", name, path,
            self._config_item_block(VPN_CERTIFICATE_CRL_SCOPE, name, [value]),
        )
        return True

    def _submit_tftp_fallback(self):
        kind, name, path = self._current_item
        if kind == "local":
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Failed to install local certificate '{name}' through config; "
                "TFTP cannot import separate private-key and certificate files"
            )
        filename = name
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", filename):
            filename = f"pki-{kind}-{self._indexes[kind]:03d}"
        os.makedirs(self._staging_directory, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(path, os.path.join(self._staging_directory, filename))
        self._fallback_active = True
        self.commander.submit_block(self, CommandSequence(f"{kind}-tftp-fallback", [
            CommandSpec(
                f"execute vpn certificate {kind} import tftp "
                f"pki/{filename} {self._tftp_server_ip}",
                capture_output=True,
                # Let on_command_executed produce the object-specific error
                # that identifies both failed installation paths.
                fail_on_error=False,
            ),
        ]))

    @staticmethod
    def _crl_basename(path):
        return os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]

    def on_command_executed(self, command, state):
        if not command.spec.capture_output or not COMMAND_FAILURE_PATTERN.search(
            bytes(command.output)
        ):
            return
        if self._fallback_active:
            kind, name, _path = self._current_item
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Failed to install {kind} PKI object '{name}' through config "
                "and TFTP"
            )
        if self._current_item is not None:
            self._config_failed = True

    @staticmethod
    def _crl_config_from_major(major):
        # ``config vpn certificate crl`` exists from 7.0; earlier releases
        # expose no CRL CLI at all.
        return VPN_CERTIFICATE_CRL_SCOPE if major >= 7 else None

    def on_block_complete(self):
        if self._fallback_active:
            kind, name, _path = self._current_item
            self._logger.warning(
                "Installed %s PKI object '%s' through TFTP after config installation failed",
                kind,
                name,
            )
            self._fallback_active = False
            self._config_failed = False
            self._current_item = None
            self._submit_next()
            return
        if self._config_failed:
            self._submit_tftp_fallback()
            return
        self._current_item = None
        self._submit_next()

    @property
    def completion_message(self):
        return None

"""Generated end-to-end boundary cases for the FortiOS serial parser stack."""

import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import CommandSpec, SessionLossAction  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.common import Credentials, FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver import FOSCliDriver  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.terminal import Terminal  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.tests.test_common_stack_parsing import (  # noqa: E402
    SerialConnection,
)


class BoundaryFeature(Feature):
    def __init__(self, commander, spec):
        super().__init__(None, commander, "boundary-probe")
        self.spec = spec
        self.outputs = []
        self.dispatched = []

    def activate(self):
        self.commander.submit_block(self, self.spec)

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)
        self.dispatched.append(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
        self.outputs.append((bytes(attempt.output), state))

    def on_session_loss(self, attempt):
        return SessionLossAction.CONTINUE


def make_stack(spec, response, *, allow_recovery=False, initial_prompt=b"fw #"):
    logger = MagicMock()
    connection = SerialConnection({
        b"admin\r": b"Password:",
        b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\n" + initial_prompt + b"\r\n",
        b"probe\r": response,
    })
    terminal = Terminal(connection, logger, default_wait="fw #")
    commander = FOSCommander(terminal, logger)
    feature = BoundaryFeature(commander, spec)
    commander.start([feature])
    driver = FOSCliDriver(
        terminal,
        commander,
        Credentials("admin", "secret"),
        logger,
        "Bootstrap1!",
        MagicMock(),
        MagicMock(),
        allow_credential_recovery=allow_recovery,
    )
    if allow_recovery:
        driver.remember_current_credentials()
    states = []
    original_on_state = commander.on_state
    def record_state(state, output):
        states.append(state)
        return original_on_state(state, output)
    commander.on_state = record_state
    original_echo = commander.on_prompt_echo
    def record_echo(output):
        states.append(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO)
        return original_echo(output)
    commander.on_prompt_echo = record_echo
    return connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states

def prompt_case(hostname, context, marker, ending):
    prompt = hostname + context + " " + marker
    response = (
        (prompt + " probe" + ending + "captured diagnostic" + ending + prompt + ending)
        .encode()
    )
    spec = CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True)
    connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states = make_stack(
        spec, response, initial_prompt=prompt.encode()
    )
    try:
        with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
            driver.process_state()
        assert commander.ready
        assert feature.completed
        assert feature.outputs[0][1] == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT
        assert b"captured diagnostic" in feature.outputs[0][0]
        assert FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO in states
    finally:
        if not connection.closed:
            terminal.close()


def state_case(state, sample, suffix=b"", *, recover=False):
    response = sample + suffix
    if state in (FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_REJECTED, FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME):
        completion = (FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT,)
    elif state in (FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED, FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO):
        completion = (FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT,)
    else:
        completion = (state,)
    connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states = make_stack(
        CommandSpec("probe", completion_states=completion, capture_output=True),
        response,
        allow_recovery=recover,
        initial_prompt=b"fw (global) #" if state == FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO else b"fw #",
    )
    try:
        with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.03), \
                patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
            driver.process_state()
        assert state in states
        assert commander.ready
        assert feature.completed
    finally:
        if not connection.closed:
            terminal.close()


class EndToEndBoundaryCases(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_expected_completion_prompt_mismatch_raises_from_serial_result(self):
        response = b"Do you want to continue?\r\n"
        connection, terminal, _commander, driver, _feature, _states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec(
                "probe",
                completion_states=(FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT),
                expected_completion_state=FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT,
            ),
            response,
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "expected CMD_PROMPT, received CONFIRMATION"):
                    driver.process_state()
        finally:
            terminal.close()

    def test_error_text_is_captured_when_fail_on_error_is_disabled(self):
        response = b"Command fail. Return code -542\r\nfw #\r\n"
        connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, _states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True, fail_on_error=False), response
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
            self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
            self.assertIn(b"Command fail. Return code -542", feature.outputs[0][0])
        finally:
            if not connection.closed:
                terminal.close()

    def test_noise_without_a_pattern_reaches_unknown_then_timeout(self):
        connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True), b"\xff\x00garbage\r\nnot-a-prompt\r\n"
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.01), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 0.06):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertIn(FOSCliState.UNKNOWN, states)
            self.assertIn(FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT, states)
            self.assertFalse(commander.ready)
            self.assertFalse(feature.completed)
            self.assertIn(b"garbage", bytes(feature.current_attempt.output))
        finally:
            terminal.close()

    def test_idle_read_exposes_retained_prompt_newline(self):
        connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True), None
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.01), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 0.04):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertIn(FOSCliState.TN_TIMEOUT, states)
            # The login response ended with a newline after the matched CLI
            # prompt. Full-buffer timeout inspection exposes that real byte.
            self.assertEqual(bytes(feature.current_attempt.output), b"\n")
            self.assertTrue(commander.busy)
        finally:
            terminal.close()

    def test_partial_prompt_and_command_echo_are_buffered_across_reads(self):
        command_echo = b"fw (global) # probe\r\n"
        payload = b"config system dns\r\n set primary 1.1.1.1\r\nend\r\nfw (global) #\r\n"
        response = tuple([command_echo[:3], command_echo[3:12], command_echo[12:] + payload[:11], payload[11:29], payload[29:]])
        connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True), response,
            initial_prompt=b"fw (global) #",
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
            self.assertIn(FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO, states)
            self.assertIn(b"set primary 1.1.1.1", feature.outputs[0][0])
        finally:
            if not connection.closed:
                terminal.close()


# Exercise every pattern-backed state through the real terminal, driver, and
# commander. States that represent a login transition include the follow-up
# prompt needed for the real scheduler to safely finish the feature.
STATE_CASES = [
    ("username_prompt", FOSCliState.PROVIDE_USERNAME, b"fw login:\r\n", b"Password:\r\nWelcome!\r\nfw #\r\n", False),
    ("password_prompt", FOSCliState.PROVIDE_PASSWORD, b"Password:", b"", False),
    ("new_password_prompt", FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD, b"New Password:", b"", False),
    ("credential_rejected", FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_REJECTED, b"Login incorrect\r\n", b"fw login:\r\nPassword:\r\nWelcome!\r\nfw #\r\n", True),
    ("credential_accepted", FOSCliState.CREDENTIAL_ACCEPTED, b"Welcome!\r\n", b"fw #\r\n", False),
    ("license_failure_notice", FOSCliState.LIC_FAIL, b"VM license install failed.\r\n", b"", False),
    ("command_prompt", FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT, b"fw #\r\n", b"", False),
    ("command_prompt_echo", FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT_ECHO, b"fw (global) # probe\r\n", b"fw (global) #\r\n", False),
    ("shutdown_notice", FOSCliState.SHUTTING_DOWN, b"system is going down\r\n", b"", False),
    ("reboot_notice", FOSCliState.REBOOTING, b"stand by while rebooting\r\n", b"", False),
    ("session_lost_notice", FOSCliState.SESSION_LOST, b"*ATTENTION*: Admin sessions removed because license registration status changed\r\n", b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n", False),
    ("current_password_prompt", FOSCliState.CURRENT_PASSWORD, b"Current Password:\r\n", b"", False),
    ("confirmation_prompt", FOSCliState.CONFIRMATION, b"Do you want to continue?\r\n", b"", False),
    ("confirm_new_password_prompt", FOSCliState.CHANGE_PASSWORD_CONFIRM, b"Confirm Password:\r\n", b"", False),
    ("pager_prompt", FOSCliState.MORE_PROMPT, b"--More--", b"", False),
    ("multiline_prompt", FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT, b">\r\n", b"", False),
]


def _make_state_test(case):
    name, state, sample, suffix, recover = case
    def test(self):
        with self.subTest(state=state.name):
            state_case(state, sample, suffix, recover=recover)
    test.__name__ = f"test_state_{name}_through_full_stack"
    test.__doc__ = f"Reach {state.name} from connection bytes and observe commander handling."
    return test


for _case in STATE_CASES:
    setattr(EndToEndBoundaryCases, f"test_state_{_case[0]}_through_full_stack", _make_state_test(_case))


# Hostname, prompt context, prompt glyph, and line ending are independent
# parser boundaries. The Cartesian set creates one discoverable test per wire
# shape so failures point to the exact prompt form.
PROMPT_CASES = [
    (host, context, marker, ending)
    for host in ("fw", "edge-01", "FortiGate-VM64-KVM", "FGVMABC123")
    for context in ("", " (global)", " (root) (vdom blue)")
    for marker in ("#", "$")
    for ending in ("\n", "\r\n")
]


def _make_prompt_test(case):
    hostname, context, marker, ending = case
    label = f"{hostname}_{context or 'plain'}_{marker}_{'crlf' if ending == chr(13)+chr(10) else 'lf'}"
    def test(self):
        prompt_case(hostname, context, marker, ending)
    test.__name__ = "test_prompt_" + "_".join(part.replace(" ", "").replace("(", "").replace(")", "") for part in label.split("_"))
    test.__doc__ = f"Parse command echo and prompt {hostname}{context} {marker} with {ending!r}."
    return test


for _case in PROMPT_CASES:
    setattr(EndToEndBoundaryCases, _make_prompt_test(_case).__name__, _make_prompt_test(_case))


# Distinct failure payloads ensure the command failure parser handles signed
# and unsigned return codes and optional whitespace over the serial boundary.
ERROR_CASES = [b"0", b"1", b"-1", b"-5", b"-542", b"255", b"0007", b"-214"]


def _make_failure_test(return_code):
    def test(self):
        response = b"Command fail. Return code " + return_code + b"\r\nfw #\r\n"
        connection, terminal, _commander, driver, _feature, _states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True, fail_on_error=True), response
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, f"return code {return_code.decode()}"):
                    driver.process_state()
        finally:
            terminal.close()
    test.__name__ = f"test_command_error_code_{return_code.decode().replace('-', 'negative_')}"
    test.__doc__ = f"Pass FortiOS return code {return_code.decode()} through the full stack."
    return test


for _code in ERROR_CASES:
    setattr(EndToEndBoundaryCases, _make_failure_test(_code).__name__, _make_failure_test(_code))


CAPTURE_CASES = [
    b"one line\n",
    b"multiple\nlines\nwith trailing newline\n",
    b"carriage return\rwithout line feed",
    b"\xff\xfe\x00binary-ish bytes",
    b"\x1b[31mcolored output\x1b[0m",
    b"tabs\tand    repeated spaces",
    b"# metadata-looking output",
    b"prompt-like value fw (global) # inside data",
    b"empty-looking\n\nline",
    b"unicode utf-8: \xe2\x98\x83",
    b"long" * 2048,
    b"return code text: Command fail. Return code -7",
]


def _make_capture_test(index, payload):
    def test(self):
        ending = b"\r\n"
        response = payload + ending + b"fw #\r\n"
        connection, terminal, commander, driver, feature, _states = make_stack(
            CommandSpec("probe", capture_output=True), response
        )
        try:
            with patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.EXPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.05), \
                    patch("fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver.PROCESS_SPIN_SECONDS", 1):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
            self.assertEqual(feature.outputs[0][1], FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)
            self.assertIn(payload, feature.outputs[0][0])
        finally:
            if not connection.closed:
                terminal.close()
    test.__name__ = f"test_capture_payload_{index:02d}"
    test.__doc__ = f"Capture serial output payload case {index}."
    return test


for _index, _payload in enumerate(CAPTURE_CASES):
    setattr(EndToEndBoundaryCases, f"test_capture_payload_{_index:02d}", _make_capture_test(_index, _payload))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""End-to-end parsing from a serial connection through the FortiOS commander."""

import queue
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from fortinet.common.cli_commands import (  # noqa: E402
    CommandSequence, CommandSpec, ConfigBlock, EditBlock, SetValue,
)
from fortinet.common.common import Credentials, FOSCliState  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.features.base import Feature  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_cli_driver import FOSCliDriver  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.fos_commander import FOSCommander  # noqa: E402
from fortinet.common.terminal import Terminal  # noqa: E402


class SerialConnection:
    """A serial-like connection that answers each write with a byte stream."""

    def __init__(self, responses):
        self._incoming = queue.Queue()
        self._responses = responses
        self.writes = []
        self.closed = False
        self._incoming.put(b"fw login:\r\n")

    def read_very_eager(self):
        try:
            return self._incoming.get_nowait()
        except queue.Empty:
            return b""

    def write(self, data):
        data = bytes(data)
        self.writes.append(data)
        response = self._responses.get(data)
        if callable(response):
            response = response()
        if response:
            chunks = response if isinstance(response, (tuple, list)) else (response,)
            for chunk in chunks:
                if chunk:
                    self._incoming.put(bytes(chunk))

    def close(self):
        self.closed = True

    def suppress_output(self):
        from contextlib import nullcontext
        return nullcontext()


class RecordingFeature(Feature):
    def __init__(self, commander, name, commands):
        super().__init__(None, commander, name)
        self.commands = commands
        self.executed = []
        self.dispatched = []

    def activate(self):
        self.commander.submit_block(self, CommandSequence(self.name, self.commands))

    def on_command_dispatched(self, attempt):
        super().on_command_dispatched(attempt)
        self.dispatched.append(attempt)

    def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
        self.executed.append((attempt.spec.line, bytes(attempt.output), state))


class FullStackParsingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def make_stack(self, features, responses, *, allow_credential_recovery=False):
        logger = MagicMock()
        connection = SerialConnection(responses)
        terminal = Terminal(connection, logger, default_wait="fw #")
        commander = FOSCommander(terminal, logger)
        commander.start(features(commander))
        driver = FOSCliDriver(
            terminal=terminal,
            commander=commander,
            credentials=Credentials("admin", "secret"),
            logger=logger,
            bootstrap_password="Bootstrap1!",
            activate_blank_credentials=MagicMock(),
            activate_bootstrap_credentials=MagicMock(),
            allow_credential_recovery=allow_credential_recovery,
        )
        return connection, terminal, commander, driver

    def test_login_command_echo_multiline_output_and_continuation(self):
        result = b"".join([
            b"fw # show full-configuration system dns\r\n",
            b"config system dns\r\n",
            b"    set protocol dot\r\n",
            b"    set primary 9.9.9.9\r\n",
            b"end\r\n",
            b"fw #\r\n",
        ])
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n",
            b"show full-configuration system dns\r": result,
            b'set comment "first line\r': b">\r\n",
            b"second line\r": b">\r\n",
            b'third line"\r': b"fw #\r\n",
        }
        features = []

        def configured(commander):
            inspect = RecordingFeature(commander, "inspect", [
                CommandSpec("show full-configuration system dns", capture_output=True),
            ])
            multiline = RecordingFeature(commander, "multiline", [
                SetValue("comment", "first line\nsecond line\nthird line"),
            ])
            features.extend([inspect, multiline])
            return features

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        driver.process_state()

        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
        self.assertTrue(commander.startup_complete)
        self.assertTrue(all(feature.completed for feature in features))
        self.assertTrue(connection.closed)
        self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
            b"admin\r",
            b"secret\r",
            b"show full-configuration system dns\r",
            b'set comment "first line\r',
            b"second line\r",
            b'third line"\r',
        ])
        self.assertEqual(len(features[0].executed), 1)
        captured = features[0].executed[0][1]
        self.assertIn(b"set protocol dot", captured)
        self.assertIn(b"set primary 9.9.9.9", captured)
        self.assertEqual(features[0].executed[0][2], FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry[2] for entry in features[1].executed],
            [FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT, FOSCliState.MULTILINE_PROMPT, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT],
        )
        self.assertTrue(all(attempt.output for attempt in features[1].dispatched))
        self.assertEqual(bytes(terminal._buffer), b"")

    def test_mixed_prompt_context_and_pager_states_reach_feature_callbacks(self):
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw (global) #\r\n",
            b"get system status\r": (
                b"fw (global) # get system status\r\n"
                b"Version: FortiGate-VM64 v7.4.2,build2571\r\n"
                b"--More--\r\n"
                b"Serial-Number: FGVMTEST\r\n"
                b"fw (global) #\r\n"
            ),
            b" \r": b"fw (global) #\r\n",
        }
        feature_ref = []

        class PagerFeature(RecordingFeature):
            def on_command_executed(self, attempt, state):
                super().on_command_executed(attempt, state)
                self.commander.feature_complete(self)

        def configured(commander):
            feature = PagerFeature(commander, "status", [
                CommandSpec("get system status", capture_output=True),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, _terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        driver.process_state()

        feature = feature_ref[0]
        self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
        self.assertTrue(feature.completed)
        self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
            b"admin\r", b"secret\r", b"get system status\r", b" ",
        ])
        captured = feature.executed[0][1]
        self.assertIn(b"FortiGate-VM64 v7.4.2,build2571", captured)
        self.assertIn(b"Serial-Number: FGVMTEST", captured)
        self.assertEqual(feature.executed[0][2], FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)
        self.assertEqual(driver._current_state, FOSCliState.CMD_PROMPT)

    def test_aborted_interface_edit_recovers_through_serial_driver(self):
        ip_responses = iter([
            b"abort\r\nfw (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
        ])
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"config system interface\r": b"fw (interface) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"edit port1\r": b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r": lambda: next(ip_responses),
            b"set allowaccess ping https ssh http\r": b"fw (port1) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"next\r": b"fw (interface) (Interim)#\r\n",
            b"end\r": b"fw (Interim)#\r\n",
        }
        feature_ref = []

        def configured(commander):
            feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "management", [
                ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", [
                    "set ip 10.0.52.4/24", "set allowaccess ping https ssh http",
                ])]),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        try:
            driver.process_state()
            self.assertTrue(commander.ready)
            self.assertTrue(feature_ref[0].completed)
            self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
                b"admin\r", b"secret\r",
                b"config system interface\r", b"edit port1\r", b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r",
                b"config system interface\r", b"edit port1\r", b"set ip 10.0.52.4/24\r",
                b"set allowaccess ping https ssh http\r", b"next\r", b"end\r",
            ])
        finally:
            terminal.close()

    def test_failed_next_ejects_before_end_through_serial_driver(self):
        responses = {
            b"admin\r": b"Password:",
            b"secret\r": b"Welcome!\r\nfw #\r\n",
            b"config system interface\r": b"fw (interface)#\r\n",
            b"edit port1\r": b"fw (port1)#\r\n",
            b"set unsupported 1\r": b"Command fail. Return code -61.\r\nfw (port1)#\r\n",
            b"next\r": (
                b"Command fa", b"il. Return code -5.\r\nfw (port1)#\r\n",
            ),
        }
        feature_ref = []

        def configured(commander):
            feature = RecordingFeature(commander, "management", [
                ConfigBlock("system interface", [EditBlock("port1", ["set unsupported 1"])]),
            ])
            feature_ref.append(feature)
            return [feature]

        connection, terminal, commander, driver = self.make_stack(configured, responses)
        try:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "'next'.*return code -5"):
                driver.process_state()
            self.assertEqual(connection.writes, [
                b"admin\r", b"secret\r", b"config system interface\r",
                b"edit port1\r", b"set unsupported 1\r", b"next\r",
            ])
            self.assertFalse(feature_ref[0].completed)
            self.assertFalse(commander.ready)
        finally:
            terminal.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
